Whoever, being legally bound by an oath or affirmation to state the truth on any subject to any public servant or other person authorized by law to administer such oath or affirmation, makes, to such public servant or other person or as aforesaid, touching that subject, any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.182.title: False information with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to the injury of another person

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - False information with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to the injury of another person: 182.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding false information with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to the injury of another person.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.182.full_text:
182. Whoever gives to any public servant any information which he knows or believes to be false, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, such public servant
(a) to do or omit anything which such public servant ought not to do or omit if the true state of facts respecting which such information is given were known by him, or
(b) to use the lawful power of such public servant to the injury or annoyance of any person,
shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.
Illustrations
(a) A informs a Magistrate that Z, a police officer, subordinate to such Magistrate, has been guilty of neglect of duty or misconduct knowing such information to be false, and knowing it to be likely that the information will cause the Magistrate to dismiss Z. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
(b) A falsely informs a public servant that Z has contraband salt in a secret place, knowing such information to be false, and knowing that it is likely that the consequence of the information will be a search of Z's premises, attended with annoyance to Z. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
(c) A falsely informs a policeman that he has been assaulted and robbed in the neighborhood of a particular village. He does not mention the name of any person as one of his assailants, but knows it to be likely that in consequence of this information the police will make enquiries and institute searches in the village to the annoyance of the villagers or some of them. A has committed an offence under this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.183.title: Resistance to the taking of property by the lawful authority of a public servant

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Resistance to the taking of property by the lawful authority of a public servant: 183.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding resistance to the taking of property by the lawful authority of a public servant.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.183.full_text: 183. Whoever offers any resistance to the taking of any property by the lawful authority of any public servant, knowing or having reason to believe that he is such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.184.title: Obstructing sale of property offered for sale by authority of public servant

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Obstructing sale of property offered for sale by authority of public servant: 184.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding obstructing sale of property offered for sale by authority of public servant.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.184.full_text: 184. Whoever intentionally obstructs any sale of property offered for sale by the lawful authority of any public servant, as such, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.185.title: Illegal purchase or bid for property offered for sale by authority of public servant

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Illegal purchase or bid for property offered for sale by authority of public servant: 185.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding illegal purchase or bid for property offered for sale by authority of public servant.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.185.full_text: 185. Whoever, at any sale of property held by the lawful authority of a public servant, as such, purchases or bids for any property on account of any person, whether himself or any other, whom he knows to be under a legal incapacity to purchase that property at that sale, or bids for such property not intending to perform the obligations under which he lays himself by such bidding, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to two hundred taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.186.title: Obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions: 186.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.186.full_text: 186. Whoever voluntarily obstructs any public servant in the discharge of his public functions, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.187.title: Omission to assist public servant when bound by law to give assistance

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Omission to assist public servant when bound by law to give assistance: 187.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding omission to assist public servant when bound by law to give assistance.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.187.full_text:
187. Whoever, being bound by law to render or furnish assistance to any public servant in the execution of his public duty, intentionally omits to give such assistance, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to two hundred taka, or with both;
and if such assistance be demanded of him by a public servant legally competent to make such demand for the purposes of executing any process lawfully issued by a Court of Justice, or of preventing the commission of an offence, or of suppressing a riot, or affray, or of apprehending a person charged with or guilty of an offence, or of having escaped from lawful custody, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.188.title: Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant: 188.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.188.full_text:
188. Whoever, knowing that, by an order promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered to promulgate such order, he is directed to abstain from a certain act, or to take certain order with certain property in his possession or under his management, disobeys such direction,
shall, if such disobedience causes or tends to cause obstruction, annoyance or injury, or risk of obstruction, annoyance or injury, to any persons lawfully employed, be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month or with fine which may extend to two hundred taka, or with both;
and if such disobedience causes or tends to cause danger to human life, health or safety, or causes or tends to cause a riot or affray, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.
Explanation.-It is not necessary that the offender should intend to produce harm, or contemplate his disobedience as likely to produce harm. It is sufficient that he knows of the order which he disobeys, and that his disobedience produces, or is likely to produce, harm.
Illustration
An order is promulgated by a public servant lawfully empowered to promulgate such order, directing that a religious procession shall not pass down a certain street. A knowingly disobeys the order, and thereby causes danger of riot. A has committed the offence defined in this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.189.title: Threat of injury to public servant

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Threat of injury to public servant: 189.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding threat of injury to public servant.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.189.full_text: 189. Whoever holds out any threat of injury to any public servant, or to any person in whom he believes that public servant to be interested, for the purpose of inducing that public servant to do any act, or to forbear or delay to do any act, connected with the exercise of the public functions of such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.190.title: Threat of injury to induce person to refrain from applying for protection to public servant

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Threat of injury to induce person to refrain from applying for protection to public servant: 190.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding threat of injury to induce person to refrain from applying for protection to public servant.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.190.full_text: 190. Whoever holds out any threat of injury to any person for the purpose of inducing that person to refrain or desist from making a legal application for protection against any injury to any public servant legally empowered as such to give such protection, or to cause such protection to be given, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.191.title: Giving false evidence

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Giving false evidence: 191.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding giving false evidence.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.191.full_text:
191. Whoever being legally bound by an oath or by an express provision of law to state the truth, or being bound by law to make a declaration upon any subject, makes any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, is said to give false evidence.Explanation 1.-A statement is within the meaning of this section, whether it is made verbally or otherwise.
Explanation 2.-A false statement as to the belief of the person attesting is within the meaning of this section, and a person may be guilty of giving false evidence by stating that he believes a thing which he does not believe, as well as by stating that he knows a thing which he does not know.
Illustrations
(a) A, in support of a just claim which B has against Z for one thousand taka falsely swears on a trial that he heard Z admit the justice of B's claim, A has given false evidence.
(b) A, being bound by an oath to state the truth, states that he believes a certain signature to be the handwriting of Z, when he does not believe it to be the handwriting of Z. Here A states that which he knows to be false, and therefore gives false evidence.
(c) A, Knowing the general character of Z's handwriting, states that he believes a certain signature to be the handwriting of Z; A in good faith believing it to be so. Here A's statement is merely as to his belief, and is true as to his belief, and therefore, although the signature may not be the handwriting of Z, A has not given false evidence.
(d) A, being bound by an oath to state the truth, states that he knows that Z was at a particular place on a particular day, not knowing anything upon the subject. A gives false evidence whether Z was at that place on the day named or not.
(e) A, an interpreter or translator, gives or certifies as a true interpretation or translation of a statement of document, which he is bound by oath to interpret or translate truly, that which is not and which he does not believe to be a true interpretation or translation. A has given false evidence.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.192.title: Fabricating false evidence

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Fabricating false evidence: 192.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding fabricating false evidence.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.192.full_text:
192. Whoever causes any circumstance to exist or makes any false entry in any book or record, or makes any document containing a false statement, intending that such circumstance, false entry or false statement may appear in evidence in a judicial proceeding, or in a proceeding taken by law before
a public servant as such, or before an arbitrator, and that such
circumstance, false entry or false statement, so appearing in evidence, may cause any person who in such proceeding is to form an opinion upon the evidence, to entertain an erroneous opinion touching any point material to the result of such proceeding, is said "to fabricate the evidence.”
Illustrations
(a) A puts jewels into a box belonging to Z, with the intention that they may be found in that box, and that this circumstance may cause Z to be convicted of theft. A has fabricated false evidence.
(b) A makes a false entry in his Shop-book for the purpose of using it as corroborative evidence in a Court of Justice. A has fabricated false evidence.
(c) A, with the intention of causing Z to be convicted of a criminal conspiracy, writes a letter in imitation of Z's handwriting purporting to be addressed to an accomplice in such criminal conspiracy, and puts the letter in a place which he knows that the officers of the Police are likely to search. A has fabricated false evidence.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.193.title: Punishment for false evidence

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment for false evidence: 193.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment for false evidence.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.193.full_text:
193. Whoever intentionally gives false evidence in any stage of judicial proceeding, or fabricates false evidence for the purpose of being used in any stage of a judicial proceeding, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine;
and whoever intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence in any other case, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation 1.-A trial before a Court-martial is a judicial proceeding.
Explanation 2.-An investigation directed by law preliminary to a proceeding before a Court of Justice, is a stage of a judicial proceeding, though that investigation may not take place before a Court of Justice.
Illustration
A, in an enquiry before a Magistrate for the purpose of ascertaining whether Z ought to be committed for trial, makes on oath a statement which he knows to be false. As this enquiry is a stage of a judicial proceeding. A has given false evidence.
Explanation 3.-An investigation directed by a Court of Justice according to law, and conducted under the authority of a Court of Justice, is a stage of a judicial proceeding, though that investigation may not take place before a Court of Justice.
Illustration
A, in an enquiry before an officer deputed by a Court of Justice to ascertain on the spot the boundaries of land, makes on oath a statement which he knows to be false. As this enquiry is a stage of a judicial proceeding, A has given false evidence.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.194.title: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence; if innocent person be thereby convicted and executed

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence; if innocent person be thereby convicted and executed: 194.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence; if innocent person be thereby convicted and executed.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.194.full_text:
194. Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence, intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, any person to be convicted of an offence which is capital by any law for the time being in force, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine;
and if an innocent person be convicted and executed in consequence of such false evidence, the person who gives such false evidence shall be punished either with death or the punishment herein before described.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.195.title: Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment: 195.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.195.full_text:
195. Whoever gives or fabricates false evidence intending thereby to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, any person to be convicted of an offence which by any law for the time being in force is not capital, but punishable with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term of seven
years or upwards, shall be punished as a person convicted of that offence would be liable to be punished.
 
 
Illustration
A gives false evidence before a Court of Justice, intending thereby to cause Z to be convicted of a dacoity. The punishment of dacoity is imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, with or without fine. A, therefore, is liable to such imprisonment for life or imprisonment, with or without fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.196.title: Using evidence known to be false

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Using evidence known to be false: 196.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding using evidence known to be false.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.196.full_text: 196. Whoever corruptly uses or attempts to use as true or genuine evidence, any evidence which he knows to be false or fabricated, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave or fabricated false evidence.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.197.title: Issuing or signing false certificate

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Issuing or signing false certificate: 197.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding issuing or signing false certificate.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.197.full_text: 197. Whoever issues or signs any certificate required by law to be given or signed, or relating to any fact of which such certificate is by law admissible in evidence, knowing or believing that such certificate is false in any material point, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.198.title: Using as true a certificate known to be false

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Using as true a certificate known to be false: 198.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding using as true a certificate known to be false.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.198.full_text: 198. Whoever corruptly uses or attempts to use any such certificate as a true certificate, knowing the same to be false in any material point, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.199.title: False statement made in declaration which is by law receivable as evidence

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - False statement made in declaration which is by law receivable as evidence: 199.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding false statement made in declaration which is by law receivable as evidence.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.199.full_text: 199. Whoever, in any declaration made or subscribed by him, which declaration any Court of Justice, or any public servant or other persons, is bound or authorized by law to receive as evidence of any fact, makes any statement which is false, and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, touching any point material to the object for which the declaration is made or used, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.200.title: Using as true such declaration knowing it to be false

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Using as true such declaration knowing it to be false: 200.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding using as true such declaration knowing it to be false.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.200.full_text:
200. Whoever corruptly uses or attempts to use as true any such declaration, knowing the same to be false in any material point, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence.
Explanation.-A declaration which is inadmissible merely upon the ground of some informality, is a declaration within the meaning of sections 199 and 200.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.201.title: Causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information to screen offender- if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life; if punishable with less than ten years’ imprisonment

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information to screen offender- if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life; if punishable with less than ten years’ imprisonment: 201.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information to screen offender- if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life; if punishable with less than ten years’ imprisonment.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.202.title: Intentional omission to give information of offence by person bound to inform

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Intentional omission to give information of offence by person bound to inform: 202.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding intentional omission to give information of offence by person bound to inform.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.202.full_text: 202. Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed, intentionally omits to give any information respecting that offence which he is legally bound to give, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.203.title: Giving false information respecting an offence committed

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Giving false information respecting an offence committed: 203.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding giving false information respecting an offence committed.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.203.full_text:
203. Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that an offence has been committed, gives any information respecting that offence which he knows or believes to be false, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
Explanation.-In sections 201 and 202 and in this section the word "offence" includes any act committed at any place out of Bangladesh, which, if committed in Bangladesh, would be punishable under any of the following sections, namely, 302, 304, 382, 392, 393, 394, 395, 396, 397, 398, 399, 402, 435, 436, 449, 450, 457, 458, 459 and 460.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.204.title: Destruction of document to prevent its production as evidence

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Destruction of document to prevent its production as evidence: 204.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding destruction of document to prevent its production as evidence.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.204.full_text: 204. Whoever secrets or destroys any document which he may be lawfully compelled to produce as evidence in a Court of Justice, or in any proceeding lawfully held before a public servant, as such, or obliterates or renders illegible the whole or any part of such document with the intention of preventing the same from being produced or used as evidence before such Court or public servant as aforesaid, or after he shall have been lawfully summoned or required to produce the same for that purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.205.title: False personation for purpose of act or proceeding in suit or prosecution

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - False personation for purpose of act or proceeding in suit or prosecution: 205.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding false personation for purpose of act or proceeding in suit or prosecution.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.205.full_text: 205. Whoever falsely personates another, and in such assumed character makes any admission or statement, or confesses judgment, or causes any process to be issued or becomes bail or security, or does any other act in any suit or criminal prosecution, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.206.title: Fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution: 206.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.206.full_text: 206. Whoever fraudulently removes, conceals, transfers or delivers to any person any property or any interest therein, intending thereby to prevent that property or interest therein from being taken as a forfeiture or in satisfaction of a fine, under a sentence which has been pronounced, or which he knows to be likely to be pronounced, by a Court of Justice or other competent authority, or from being taken in execution of a decree or order which has been made, or which he knows to be likely to be made by a Court of Justice in a civil suit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.207.title: Fraudulent claim to property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Fraudulent claim to property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution: 207.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding fraudulent claim to property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.207.full_text: 207. Whoever fraudulently accepts, receives or claims any property or any interest therein, knowing that he has no right or rightful claim to such property or interest, or practices any deception touching any right to any property or any interest therein, intending thereby to prevent that property or interest therein from being taken as a forfeiture or in satisfaction of a fine, under a sentence which has been pronounced, or which he knows to be likely to be pronounced by a Court of Justice or other competent authority, or from being taken in execution of a decree or order which has been made, or which he knows to be likely to be made by a Court of Justice in a civil suit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.208.title: Fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due: 208.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding fraudulently suffering decree for sum not due.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.208.full_text:
208. Whoever fraudulently causes or suffers a decree or order to be passed against him at the suit of any person for a sum not due, or for a larger sum than is due to such person or for any property or interest in property to which such person is not entitled, or fraudulently causes or suffers a decree or order to be executed against him after it has been satisfied, or for anything in respect of which it has been satisfied, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
Illustration
A institutes a suit against Z. Z, knowing that A is likely to obtain a decree against him fraudulently suffers a judgment to pass against him for a larger amount at the suit of B, who has no just claim against him, in order that B, either on his own account or for the benefit of Z, may share in the proceeds of any sale of Z's property which may be made under A's decree. Z has committed an offence under this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.209.title: Dishonestly making false claim in Court

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Dishonestly making false claim in Court: 209.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding dishonestly making false claim in court.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.209.full_text: 209. Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly, or with intent to injure or annoy any person, makes in a Court of Justice any claim which he knows to be false, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.210.title: Fraudulently obtaining decree for sum not due

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Fraudulently obtaining decree for sum not due: 210.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding fraudulently obtaining decree for sum not due.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.210.full_text: 210. Whoever fraudulently obtains a decree or order against any person for a sum not due, or for a larger sum than is due, or for any property or interest in property to which he is not entitled, or fraudulently causes a decree or order to be executed against any person after it has been satisfied or for anything in respect of which it has been satisfied, or fraudulently suffers or permits any such act to be done in his name, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.211.title: False charge of offence made with intent to injure

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - False charge of offence made with intent to injure: 211.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding false charge of offence made with intent to injure.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.211.full_text:
211. Whoever, with intent to cause injury to any person, institutes or causes to be instituted any criminal proceeding against that person, or falsely charges any person with having committed an offence, knowing that there is no just or lawful ground for such proceeding or charge against that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both;
and if such criminal proceeding be instituted on a false charge of an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for seven years or upwards, shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.212.title: Harbouring offender if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Harbouring offender if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment: 212.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding harbouring offender if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.212.full_text:
212. Whenever an offence has been committed, whoever harbours or conceals a person whom he knows or has reason to believe to be the offender, with the intention of screening him from legal punishment,
shall, if the offence is punishable with death, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine;
and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, shall be, punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine;
and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to one year, and not to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both.
"Offence" in this section includes any act committed at any place out of Bangladesh, which, if committed in Bangladesh, would be punishable under any of the following sections, namely, 302, 304, 382, 392, 393, 394, 395 396, 397, 398, 399, 402, 435, 436, 449, 450, 457, 458, 459 and 460; and every such act shall, for the purposes of this section, be deemed to be punishable as if the accused person had been guilty of it in Bangladesh.
Exception.This provision shall not extend to any case in which the harbour or concealment is by the husband or wife of the offender.
Illustration
A, knowing that B has committed dacoity, knowingly conceals B in order to screen him from legal punishment. Here, as B is liable to imprisonment for life, A is liable to imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding three years, and is also liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.213.title: Taking gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment- if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Taking gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment- if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment: 213.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding taking gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment- if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.214.title: Offering gift or restoration of property in consideration of screening offender- if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Offering gift or restoration of property in consideration of screening offender- if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment: 214.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding offering gift or restoration of property in consideration of screening offender- if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.215.title: Taking gift to help to recover stolen property, etc.

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Taking gift to help to recover stolen property, etc.: 215.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding taking gift to help to recover stolen property, etc..
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.215.full_text: 215. Whoever takes or agrees or consents to take any gratification under pretence or on account of helping any person to recover any moveable property of which he shall have been deprived by any offence punishable under this Code, shall, unless he uses all means in his power to cause the offender to be apprehended and convicted of the offence, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.216.title: Harbouring offender who has escaped from custody or whose apprehension has been ordered- if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Harbouring offender who has escaped from custody or whose apprehension has been ordered- if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment: 216.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding harbouring offender who has escaped from custody or whose apprehension has been ordered- if a capital offence; if punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.216.full_text:
216. Whenever any person convicted of or charged with an offence, being in lawful custody for that offence, escapes from such custody,
or whenever a public servant, in the exercise of the lawful power of such public servant, orders a certain person to be apprehended for an offence, whoever, knowing of such escape or order for apprehension, harbours or conceals that person with the intention of preventing him from being apprehended, shall be punished in the manner following, that is to say,
if the offence for which the person was in custody or is ordered to be apprehended is punishable with death, he shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine;
 
 
if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for ten years, he shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, with or without fine;
 
 
and if the offence is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to one year and not to ten years, he shall be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of the imprisonment provided for such offence or with fine, or with both.
“Offence” in this section includes also any act or omission of which a person is alleged to have been guilty out of Bangladesh which, if he had been guilty of it in Bangladesh, would have been punishable as an offence, and for which he is, under any law relating to extradition, or under the Fugitive Offenders Act, 1881, or otherwise, liable to be apprehended or detained in custody in Bangladesh, and every such act or omission shall, for the purpose of this section, be deemed to be punishable as if the accused person had been guilty of it in Bangladesh.
Exception.–This provision does not extend to the case in which the harbour or concealment is by the husband or wife of the person to be apprehended.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.216A.title: Penalty for harbouring robbers or dacoits

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Penalty for harbouring robbers or dacoits: 216A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding penalty for harbouring robbers or dacoits.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.216A.full_text:
216A. Whoever, knowing or having reason to believe that any persons are about to commit or have recently committed robbery or dacoity, harbours them or any of them, with the intention of facilitating the commission of such robbery or dacoity, or of screening them or any of them from punishment, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.-For the purposes of this section it is immaterial whether the robbery or dacoity is intended to be committed, or has been committed, within or without Bangladesh.
Exception.–This provision does not extend to the case in which the harbour is by the husband or wife of the offender.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.217.title: Public servant disobeying direction of law with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Public servant disobeying direction of law with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture: 217.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding public servant disobeying direction of law with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.217.full_text: 217. Whoever, being a public servant, knowingly disobeys any direction of the law as to the way in which he is to conduct himself as such public servant, intending thereby to save, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby save, any person from legal punishment, or subject him to a less punishment than that to which he is liable or with intent to save, or knowing that he is likely thereby to save, any property from forfeiture or any charge to which it is liable by law, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.218.title: Public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture: 218.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.218.full_text: 218. Whoever, being a public servant, and being as such public servant, charged with the preparation of any record or other writing, frames that record or writing in a manner which he knows to be incorrect, with intent to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby cause, loss or injury to the public or to any person, or with intent thereby to save, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby save, any person from legal punishment, or with intent to save, or knowing that he is likely thereby to save, any property from forfeiture or other charge to which it is liable by law, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.219.title: Public servant in judicial proceeding corruptly making report, etc., contrary to law

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Public servant in judicial proceeding corruptly making report, etc., contrary to law: 219.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding public servant in judicial proceeding corruptly making report, etc., contrary to law.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.219.full_text: 219. Whoever, being a public servant, corruptly or maliciously makes or pronounces in any stage of a Judicial proceeding, any report, order, verdict, or decision which he knows to be contrary to law, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.220.title: Commitment for trial or confinement by person having authority who knows that he is acting contrary to law

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Commitment for trial or confinement by person having authority who knows that he is acting contrary to law: 220.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding commitment for trial or confinement by person having authority who knows that he is acting contrary to law.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.220.full_text: 220. Whoever, being in any office which gives him legal authority to commit persons for trial or to confinement, or to keep persons in confinement, corruptly or maliciously commits any person for trial or confinement, or keeps any person in confinement, in the exercise of that authority, knowing that in so doing he is acting contrary to law, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.221.title: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend: 221.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.221.full_text:
221. Whoever, being a public servant, legally bound as such public servant to apprehend or to keep in confinement any person charged with or liable to be apprehended for an offence, intentionally omits to apprehend such person, or intentionally suffers such person to escape, or intentionally aids such person in escaping or attempting to escape from such confinement, shall be punished as follows, that is to say:
with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, with or without fine, if the person in confinement, or who ought to have been apprehended, was charged with, or liable to be apprehended for, an offence punishable with death; or
with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, with or without fine, if the person in confinement, or who ought to have been apprehended, was charged with, or liable to be apprehended for, an offence punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years; or
with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, with or without fine, if the person in confinement, or who ought to have been apprehended, was charged with, or liable to be apprehended for, an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term less than ten years.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.222.title: Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend person under sentence or lawfully committed

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend person under sentence or lawfully committed: 222.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding intentional omission to apprehend on the part of public servant bound to apprehend person under sentence or lawfully committed.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.222.full_text:
222. Whoever, being a public servant, legally bound as such public servant to apprehend or to keep in confinement any person under sentence of a Court of Justice for any offence or lawfully committed to custody, intentionally omits to apprehend such person, or intentionally suffers such person to escape or intentionally aids such person in escaping or attempting to escape from such confinement, shall be punished as follows that is to say:-
with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to fourteen years, with
or without fine, if the person in confinement, or who ought to have been apprehended, is under sentence of death; or
with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, with or without fine, if the person in confinement, or who ought to have been apprehended, is subject, by a sentence of a Court of Justice, or by virtue of a commutation of such sentence, to imprisonment for life
 
 or imprisonment for a term of ten years or upwards; or
with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both, if the person in confinement, or who ought to have been apprehended is subject, by a sentence of a Court of Justice, to imprisonment for a term not extending to ten years or if the person was lawfully committed to custody.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.223.title: Escape from confinement or custody negligently suffered by public servant

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Escape from confinement or custody negligently suffered by public servant: 223.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding escape from confinement or custody negligently suffered by public servant.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.223.full_text: 223. Whoever, being a public servant legally bound as such public servant to keep in confinement any person charged with or convicted of any offence or lawfully committed to custody, negligently suffers such persons to escape from confinement, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.224.title: Resistance or obstruction by a person to his lawful apprehension

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Resistance or obstruction by a person to his lawful apprehension: 224.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding resistance or obstruction by a person to his lawful apprehension.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.224.full_text:
224. Whoever intentionally offers any resistance or illegal obstruction to the lawful apprehension of himself for any offence with which he is charged or of which he has been convicted, or escapes or attempts to escape from any custody in which he is lawfully detained for any such offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
Explanation.-The punishment in this section is in addition to the punishment for which the person to be apprehended or detained in custody was liable for the offence with which he was charged, or of which he was convicted.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.225B.title: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension, or escape or rescue, in cases not otherwise provided for

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension, or escape or rescue, in cases not otherwise provided for: 225B.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension, or escape or rescue, in cases not otherwise provided for.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.225B.full_text: 225B. Whoever, in any case not provided for in section 224 or section 225 or in any other law for the time being in force, intentionally offers any resistance or illegal obstruction to the lawful apprehension of himself or of any other person, or escapes or attempts to escape from any custody in which he is lawfully detained, or rescues or attempts to rescue any other person from any custody in which that person is lawfully detained, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.]

BD-PENAL-1860:s.225.title: Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension of another person

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension of another person: 225.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension of another person.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.225A.title: Omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant, in cases not otherwise provided for

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant, in cases not otherwise provided for: 225A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant, in cases not otherwise provided for.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.225A.full_text:
225A. Whoever, being a public servant legally bound as such public servant to apprehend, or to keep in confinement, any person in any case not provided for in section 221, section 222 or section 223, or in any other law for the time being in force, omits to apprehend that person or suffers him to escape from confinement, shall be punished
(a) if he does so intentionally, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine or with both; and
(b) if he does so negligently, with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.227.title: Violation of condition of remission of punishment

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Violation of condition of remission of punishment: 227.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding violation of condition of remission of punishment.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.227.full_text: 227. Whoever, having accepted any conditional remission of punishment, knowingly violates any condition on which such remission was granted, shall be punished with the punishment to which he was originally sentenced, if he has already suffered no part of that punishment, and if he has suffered any part of that punishment, then with so much of that punishment as he has not already suffered.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.228.title: Intentional insult or interruption to public servant sitting in judicial proceeding

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Intentional insult or interruption to public servant sitting in judicial proceeding: 228.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding intentional insult or interruption to public servant sitting in judicial proceeding.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.228.full_text: 228. Whoever intentionally offers any insult, or causes any interruption to any public servant, while such public servant is sitting in any stage of a judicial proceeding, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.229.title: Personation of a juror or assessor

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Personation of a juror or assessor: 229.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding personation of a juror or assessor.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.229.full_text: 229. Whoever by personation or otherwise, shall intentionally cause, or knowingly suffer himself to be returned, empanelled or sworn as a juryman or assessor in any case in which he knows that he is not entitled by law to be so returned, empanelled or sworn, or knowing himself to have been so returned, empanelled or sworn contrary to law, shall voluntarily serve on such jury or as such assessor, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.230.title: “Coin” defined Bangladesh coin

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - “Coin” defined Bangladesh coin: 230.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding “coin” defined bangladesh coin.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.230.full_text:
230. Coin is metal used for the time being as money, and stamped and issued by the authority of some State or Sovereign Power in order to be so used.
Bangladesh coin is metal stamped and issued by the authority of the Government in order to be used as money; and metal which has been so stamped and issued shall continue to be Bangladesh coin for the purposes of this Chapter, notwithstanding that it may have ceased to be used as money.
Illustrations
(a) Cowries are not coin.
(b) Lumps of unstamped copper, though used as money, are not coin.
(c) Medals are not coin, inasmuch as they are not intended to be used as money.
(d) The coin denominated as the Company's taka is the Queen's coin.
(e) The "Farukhabad" taka, which was formerly used as money under the authority of the Government of India, is Bangladesh coin although it is no longer so used.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.231.title: Counterfeiting coin

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Counterfeiting coin: 231.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding counterfeiting coin.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.231.full_text:
231. Whoever counterfeits or knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.-A person commits this offence who intending to practice deception, or knowing it to be likely that deception will thereby be practiced, causes a genuine coin to appear like a different coin.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.232.title: Counterfeiting Bangladesh coin

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Counterfeiting Bangladesh coin: 232.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding counterfeiting bangladesh coin.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.232.full_text: 232. Whoever counterfeits, or knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting Bangladesh coin, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.233.title: Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting coin

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting coin: 233.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding making or selling instrument for counterfeiting coin.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.233.full_text: 233. Whoever makes or mends, or performs any part of the process of making or mending, or buys, sells or disposes of, any die or instrument, for the purpose of being used, or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used, for the purpose of counterfeiting coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.234.title: Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting Bangladesh coin

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting Bangladesh coin: 234.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding making or selling instrument for counterfeiting bangladesh coin.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.234.full_text: 234. Whoever makes or mends, or performs any part of the process of making or mending or buys, sells or disposes of, any die or instrument, for the purpose of being used, or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used, for the purpose of counterfeiting Bangladesh coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.235.title: Possession of instrument or material for the purpose of using the same for counterfeiting coin; if Bangladesh coin

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Possession of instrument or material for the purpose of using the same for counterfeiting coin; if Bangladesh coin: 235.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding possession of instrument or material for the purpose of using the same for counterfeiting coin; if bangladesh coin.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.235.full_text:
235. Whoever is in possession of any instrument or material, for the purpose of using the same for counterfeiting coin, or knowing or having reason to believe that the same is intended to be used for that purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine;
and if the coin to be counterfeited is Bangladesh coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.236.title: Abetting in Bangladesh the counterfeiting out of Bangladesh of coin

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abetting in Bangladesh the counterfeiting out of Bangladesh of coin: 236.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abetting in bangladesh the counterfeiting out of bangladesh of coin.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.236.full_text: 236. Whoever, being within Bangladesh, abets the counterfeiting of coin out of Bangladesh shall be punished in the same manner as if he abetted the counterfeiting of such coin within Bangladesh.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.237.title: Import or export of counterfeit coin

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Import or export of counterfeit coin: 237.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding import or export of counterfeit coin.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.237.full_text: 237. Whoever imports into Bangladesh, or exports therefrom, any counterfeit coin, knowingly or having reason to believe that the same is counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.238.title: Import or export of counterfeits of Bangladesh coin

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Import or export of counterfeits of Bangladesh coin: 238.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding import or export of counterfeits of bangladesh coin.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.238.full_text: 238. Whoever imports into Bangladesh, or exports therefrom, any counterfeit coin which he knows or has reason to believe to be a counterfeit of Bangladesh coin, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.239.title: Delivery of coin, possessed with knowledge that it is counterfeit

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Delivery of coin, possessed with knowledge that it is counterfeit: 239.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding delivery of coin, possessed with knowledge that it is counterfeit.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.239.full_text: 239. Whoever, having any counterfeit coin which, at the time when he became possessed of it, he knew to be counterfeit, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, delivers the same to any person, or attempts to induce any person to receive it, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.240.title: Delivery of Bangladesh coin, possessed with knowledge that it is counterfeit

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Delivery of Bangladesh coin, possessed with knowledge that it is counterfeit: 240.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding delivery of bangladesh coin, possessed with knowledge that it is counterfeit.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.240.full_text: 240. Whoever, having any counterfeit coin, which is a counterfeit of Bangladesh coin, and which, at the time when he became possessed of it, he knew to be a counterfeit of Bangladesh coin, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, delivers the same to any person, or attempts to induce any person to receive it, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.241.title: Delivery of coin as genuine, which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be counterfeit

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Delivery of coin as genuine, which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be counterfeit: 241.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding delivery of coin as genuine, which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be counterfeit.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.241.full_text:
241. Whoever delivers to any other person as genuine, or attempts to induce any other person to receive as genuine, any counterfeit coin which he knows to be counterfeit, but which he did not know to be counterfeit at the time when he took it into his possession, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine to an amount which may extend is ten times the value of the coin counterfeited, or with both.
Illustration
A, a coiner, delivers counterfeit Company's taka to his accomplice B, for the purpose of uttering them. B sells the taka to C, another, utterer, who buys them knowing them to be counterfeit. C pays away the taka for goods to D, who receives them, not knowing them to be counterfeit. D after receiving the taka, discovers that they are counterfeit and pays them away as if they were good. Here D is punishable only under this section, but B and C are punishable under section 239 or 240, as the case may be.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.242.title: Possession of counterfeit coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Possession of counterfeit coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof: 242.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding possession of counterfeit coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.242.full_text: 242. Whoever, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, is in possession of counterfeit coin, having known at the time when he became possessed thereof that such coin was counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.243.title: Possession of Bangladesh coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Possession of Bangladesh coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof: 243.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding possession of bangladesh coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.243.full_text: 243. Whoever, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, is in possession of counterfeit coin, which is a counterfeit of Bangladesh coin, having known at the time when he became possessed of it that it was counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.244.title: Person employed in mint causing coin to be of different weight or composition from that fixed by law

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Person employed in mint causing coin to be of different weight or composition from that fixed by law: 244.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding person employed in mint causing coin to be of different weight or composition from that fixed by law.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.244.full_text: 244. Whoever, being employed in any mint lawfully established in Bangladesh, does any act, or omits what he is legally bound to do, with the intention of causing any coin issued from that mint to be of a different weight or composition from the weight or composition fixed by law, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.245.title: Unlawfully taking coining instrument from mint

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Unlawfully taking coining instrument from mint: 245.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding unlawfully taking coining instrument from mint.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.245.full_text: 245. Whoever, without lawful authority, takes out of any mint, lawfully established in Bangladesh, any coining tool or instrument, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.246.title: Fraudulently or dishonesty diminishing weight or altering composition of coin

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Fraudulently or dishonesty diminishing weight or altering composition of coin: 246.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding fraudulently or dishonesty diminishing weight or altering composition of coin.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.246.full_text:
246. Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly performs on any coin any operation which diminishes the weight or alters the composition of that coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.-A person who scoops out part of the coin and puts anything else into the cavity alters the composition of that coin.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.247.title: Fraudulently or dishonestly diminishing weight or altering composition of Bangladesh coin

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Fraudulently or dishonestly diminishing weight or altering composition of Bangladesh coin: 247.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding fraudulently or dishonestly diminishing weight or altering composition of bangladesh coin.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.247.full_text: 247. Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly performs on any Bangladesh coin, any operation which diminishes the weight or alters the composition of that coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.248.title: Altering appearance of coin with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Altering appearance of coin with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description: 248.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding altering appearance of coin with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.248.full_text: 248. Whoever performs on any coin any operation which alters the appearance of that coin, with the intention that the said coin shall pass as a coin of a different description, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.249.title: Altering appearance of Bangladesh coin, with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Altering appearance of Bangladesh coin, with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description: 249.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding altering appearance of bangladesh coin, with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.249.full_text: 249. Whoever performs on any Bangladesh coin any operation which alters the appearance of that coin, with the intention that the said coin shall pass as a coin of a different description, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.250.title: Delivery of coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Delivery of coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered: 250.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding delivery of coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.250.full_text: 250. Whoever, having coin in his possession with respect to which the offence defined in section 246 or 248 has been committed, and having known at the time when he became possessed of such coin that such offence had been committed with respect to it, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, delivers such coin to any other person, or attempts to induce any other person to receive the same, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.251.title: Delivery of Bangladesh coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Delivery of Bangladesh coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered: 251.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding delivery of bangladesh coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.251.full_text: 251. Whoever, having coin in his possession with respect to which the offence defined in section 247 or 249 has been committed, and having known at the time when he became possessed of such coin that such offence had been committed with respect to it, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, delivers such coin to any other person, or attempts to induce any other person to receive the same, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.252.title: Possession of coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Possession of coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof: 252.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding possession of coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.252.full_text: 252.
