Whoever makes, or causes to be made, or uses for any purpose whatsoever, or delivers to any person, any document purporting to be, or in any way resembling, or so nearly resembling as to be calculated to deceive, any currency-note or bank-note shall be punished with fine which may extend to one hundred taka.
(2) If any person, whose name appears on a document the making of which is an offence under sub-section (1), refuses, without lawful excuse, to disclose to a police-officer on being so required the name and address of the person by whom it was printed or otherwise made, he shall be punished with fine which may extend to two hundred taka.
(3) Where the name of any person appears on any document in respect of which any person is charged with an offence under sub-section (1) or on any other document used or distributed in connection with that document it may, until the contrary is proved, be presumed that, that person caused the document to be made.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.491.title: Breach of contract to attend on and supply wants of helpless person

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Breach of contract to attend on and supply wants of helpless person: 491.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding breach of contract to attend on and supply wants of helpless person.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.491.full_text: 491. Whoever, being bound by a lawful contract to attend on or to supply the wants of any person who, by reason of youth, or of unsoundness of mind, or of a disease or bodily weakness, is helpless or incapable of providing for his own safety or of supplying his own wants, voluntarily omits so to do, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to two hundred taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.493.title: Cohabitation caused by a man deceitfully inducing a belief of lawful marriage

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Cohabitation caused by a man deceitfully inducing a belief of lawful marriage: 493.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding cohabitation caused by a man deceitfully inducing a belief of lawful marriage.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.493.full_text: 493. Every man who by deceit causes any woman who is not lawfully married to him to believe that she is lawfully married to him and to cohabit or have sexual intercourse with him in that belief, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.494.title: Marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife: 494.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.494.full_text:
494. Whoever, having a husband or wife living, marries in any case in which such marriage is void by reason of its taking place during the life of such husband or wife, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Exception.- This section does not extend to any person whose marriage with such husband or wife has been declared void by a Court of competent jurisdiction,
nor to any person who contracts a marriage during the life of a former husband or wife, if such husband or wife, at the time of the subsequent marriage, shall have been continually absent from such person for the space of seven years, and shall not have been heard of by such person as being alive within that time provided the person contracting such subsequent marriage shall, before such marriage takes place, inform the person with whom such marriage is contracted of the real state of facts so far as the same are within his or her knowledge.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.495.title: Same offence with concealment of former marriage from person with whom subsequent marriage is contracted

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Same offence with concealment of former marriage from person with whom subsequent marriage is contracted: 495.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding same offence with concealment of former marriage from person with whom subsequent marriage is contracted.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.495.full_text: 495. Whoever commits the offence defined in the last preceding section having concealed from the person with whom the subsequent marriage is contracted, the fact of the former marriage, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.496.title: Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage: 496.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.496.full_text: 496. Whoever, dishonestly or with a fraudulent intention, goes through the ceremony of being married, knowing that he is not thereby lawfully married, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.497.title: Adultery

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Adultery: 497.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding adultery.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.497.full_text: 497. Whoever has sexual intercourse with a person who is and whom he knows or has reason to believe to be the wife of anather man, without the consent or connivance of that man, such sexual intercourse not amounting to the offence of rape, is guilty of the offence of adultery, and shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both. In such case the wife shall not be punished as an abettor.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.498.title: Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman: 498.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.498.full_text: 498. Whoever takes or entices away any woman who is and whom he knows or has reason to believe to be wife of any other man, from that man, or from any person having the care of her on behalf of that man, with intent that she may have illicit intercourse with any person, or conceals or detains with that intent any such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.499.title: Defamation

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Defamation: 499.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding defamation.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.499.full_text:
499. Whoever by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or published any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm, the reputation or such person, is said, except in the cases hereinafter excepted, to defame that person.
Explanation 1.-It may amount to defamation to impute any thing to a deceased person, if the imputation would harm the reputation of that person if living, and is intended to be hurtful to the feelings of his family or other near relatives.
Explanation 2.-It may amount to defamation to make an imputation concerning a company or an association or collection of persons as such.
Explanation 3.-An imputation in the form of an alternative or expressed ironically, may amount to defamation.
Explanation 4.-No imputation is said to harm a person's reputation, unless that imputation directly or indirectly, in the estimation of others, lowers the moral or intellectual character of his caste or of his calling, or lowers the credit of that person, or causes it to be believe that body of that person is in a loathsome state, or in a state generally considered as disgraceful.
Illustrations
(a) A say's – “Z is an honest man; he never stole B's watch”; intending to cause it to be believed that Z did steal B's watch. This is defamation, unless it fall within one of the exceptions.
(b) A is asked who stole B's watch. A points to Z, intending to cause it to be believed that Z stole B's watch. This is defamation, unless it fall within one of the exceptions.
(c) A draws a picture of Z running away with B's watch, intending it to be believed that Z stole B's watch. This is defamation, unless it fall within one of the exceptions.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.500.title: Punishment for defamation

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment for defamation: 500.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment for defamation.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.500.full_text: 500. Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.501.title: Printing or engraving matter known to be defamatory

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Printing or engraving matter known to be defamatory: 501.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding printing or engraving matter known to be defamatory.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.501.full_text: 501. Whoever prints or engraves any matter, knowing or having good reason to believe that such matter is defamatory of any person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.502.title: Sale of printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Sale of printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter: 502.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding sale of printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.502.full_text: 502. Whoever sells or offers for sale any printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter, knowing that it contains such matter, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.503.title: Criminal intimidation

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Criminal intimidation: 503.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding criminal intimidation.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.503.full_text:
503. Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause to alarm to that person, or to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do any act which that person is legally entitled to do, as the means of avoiding the execution of such threat, commits criminal intimidation.
Explanation.-A threat to injure the reputation of any deceased person in whom the person threatened is interested, is within this section.
Illustration
A, for the purpose of inducing B to desist from prosecuting a civil suit, threatens to burn B's house. A is guilty of criminal intimidation.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.504.title: Intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace: 504.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.504.full_text: 504. Whoever intentionally insults, and thereby gives provocation to any person, intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause him to break the public peace, or to commit any other offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.505.title: Statements conducing to public mischief

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Statements conducing to public mischief: 505.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding statements conducing to public mischief.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.505.full_text:
505. Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement, rumour or report,
(a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the Army, Navy or Air Force of Bangladesh to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or
(b) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public or to any section of the public whereby any person may be induced to commit an offence against the state or against the public tranquility; or
(c) with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit any offence against any other class or community; or
(d) with intent to create or promote, or which is likely to create or promote, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different communities, classes or sections of people,
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
Exception.It does not amount to an offence, within the meaning of this section, when the person making, publishing or circulating any such statement, rumour or report, has reasonable grounds for believing that such statement, rumour or report is true and makes, publishes or circulates it without any such intent as aforesaid.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.505A.title: Prejudicial act by words, etc.

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Prejudicial act by words, etc.: 505A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding prejudicial act by words, etc..
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.505A.full_text:
505A. Whoever-
(a) by words, either spoken or written, or by signs or by visible representation or otherwise does anything, or
(b) makes, publishes or circulates any statement, rumour or report,
which is, or which is likely to be prejudicial to the interests of the security of Bangladesh or public order, or to the maintenance of friendly relations of Bangladesh with foreign states or to the maintenance of supplies and services essential to the community, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.506.title: Punishment for criminal intimidation

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment for criminal intimidation: 506.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment for criminal intimidation.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.506.full_text:
506. Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both;
and if the threat be to cause death or grievous hurt, or to cause the destruction of any property by fire, or to cause an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or to impute unchastity to a woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.507.title: Criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication: 507.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.507.full_text: 507. Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication, or having taken precaution to conceal the name or abode of the person from whom the threat comes, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, in addition to the punishment provided for the offence by the last preceding section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.508.title: Act caused by inducing person to believe that he will be rendered an object of the Divine displeasure

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Act caused by inducing person to believe that he will be rendered an object of the Divine displeasure: 508.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding act caused by inducing person to believe that he will be rendered an object of the divine displeasure.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.508.full_text:
508. Whoever voluntarily causes or attempts to cause any person to do anything which that person is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do anything which he is legally entitled to do, by inducing or attempting to induce that person to believe that he or any person in whom he is interested will become or will be rendered by some act of the offender an object of Divine displeasure if he does not do the thing which it is the object of the offender to cause him to do, or if he does the thing which it is the object of the offender to cause him to omit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
Illustrations
(a) A sits dhurna at Z's door with the intention of causing it to be believed that, by so sitting, he renders Z an object of Divine displeasure. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
(b) A threatens Z that, unless Z performs a certain act, A will kill one of A's own children, under such circumstances that the killing would be believed to render Z an object of Divine displeasure. A has committed the offence defined in this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.509.title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman: 509.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.509.full_text: 509. Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any word, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.510.title: Misconduct in public by a drunken person

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Misconduct in public by a drunken person: 510.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding misconduct in public by a drunken person.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.510.full_text: 510. Whoever, in a state of intoxication appears in any public place, or in any place which it is a trespass in him to enter, and there conducts himself in such a manner as to cause annoyance to any person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to twenty-four hours, or with fine which may extend to ten taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.511.title: Punishment for attempting to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment for attempting to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment: 511.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment for attempting to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life or imprisonment.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.511.full_text:
511. Whoever attempts to commit an offence punishable by this Code with imprisonment for life or imprisonment, or to cause such an offence to be committed, and in such attempt does any act towards the commission of the offence, shall, where no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such attempt, be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for that offence, or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or with both.
Illustrations
(a) A makes an attempt to steal some jewels by breaking open a box, and finds after so opening the box, that there is no jewel in it. He has done an act towards the commission of theft, and therefore is guilty under this section.
(b) A makes an attempt to pick the pocket of Z by thrusting his hand into Z's pocket. A fails in the attempt in consequence of Z's having nothing in his pocket. A is guilty under this section.

BD-CONST-1972.title: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh

BD-CONST-1972:Art.1.title: The Republic

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - The Republic: 1.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding the republic.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.1.full_text: 1. Bangladesh is a unitary, independent, sovereign Republic to be known as the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.2.title: The territory of the Republic

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - The territory of the Republic: 2.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding the territory of the republic.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.2.full_text:
2. The territory of the Republic shall comprise –
(a) the territories which immediately before the Proclamation of Independence on the 26th day of March, 1971 constituted East Pakistan and the territories referred to as included territories in the Constitution (Third Amendment) Act, 1974, but excluding the territories referred to as excluded territories in that Act; and
(b) such other territories as may become included in Bangladesh.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.2A.title: The state religion

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - The state religion: 2A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding the state religion.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.2A.full_text: 2A. The state religion of the Republic is Islam, but the State shall ensure equal status and equal right in the practice of the Hindu, Buddhist, Christian and other religions.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.3.title: The state language

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - The state language: 3.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding the state language.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.3.full_text: 3. The state language of the Republic is Bangla.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.4.title: National anthem, flag and emblem

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - National anthem, flag and emblem: 4.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding national anthem, flag and emblem.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.4.full_text:
4. (1) The national anthem of the Republic is the first ten lines of “Amar Sonar Bangla”.
(2) The national flag of the Republic shall consist of a circle, coloured red throughout its area, resting on a green background.
(3) The national emblem of the Republic is the national flower Shapla (nymphaea nouchali) resting on water, having on each side an ear of paddy and being surmounted by three connected leaves of jute with two stars on each side of the leaves.
(4) Subject to the foregoing clauses, provisions relating to the national anthem, flag and emblem shall be made by law.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.4A.title: Portrait of the Father of the Nation

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Portrait of the Father of the Nation: 4A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding portrait of the father of the nation.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.4A.full_text: 4A. The Portrait of the Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman shall be preserved and displayed at the offices of the President, the Prime Minister, the Speaker and the Chief Justice and in head and branch offices of all government and semi-government offices, autonomous bodies, statutory public authorities, government and non-government educational institutions, embassies and missions of Bangladesh abroad.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.5.title: The capital

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - The capital: 5.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding the capital.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.5.full_text:
5. (1) The capital of the Republic is Dhaka.
(2) The boundaries of the capital shall be determined by law.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.6.title: Citizenship

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Citizenship: 6.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding citizenship.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.6.full_text:
6. The citizenship of Bangladesh shall be determined and regulated by law.
(2) The people of Bangladesh shall be known as Bangalees as a nation and the citizens of Bangladesh shall be known as Bangladeshies.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.7.title: Supremacy of the Constitution

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Supremacy of the Constitution: 7.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding supremacy of the constitution.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.7.full_text:
7. (1) All powers in the Republic belong to the people, and their exercise on behalf of the people shall be effected only under, and by the authority of, this Constitution.
(2) This Constitution is, as the solemn expression of the will of the people, the supreme law of the Republic, and if any other law is inconsistent with this Constitution that other law shall, to the extent of the inconsistency, be void.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.7A.title: Offence of abrogation, suspension, etc . of the Constitution

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Offence of abrogation, suspension, etc . of the Constitution: 7A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding offence of abrogation, suspension, etc . of the constitution.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.7A.full_text:
7A. (1) If any person, by show of force or use of force or by any other un-constitutional means-

 

(a) abrogates, repeals or suspends or attempts or conspires to abrogate, repeal or suspend this Constitution or any of its article ; or

 

(b) subverts or attempts or conspires to subvert the confidence, belief or reliance of the citizens to this Constitution or any of its article,

 

his such act shall be sedition and such person shall be guilty of sedition.

 

(2) If any person-

 

(a) abets or instigates any act mentioned in clause (1) ; or

 

(b) approves, condones, supports or ratifies such act,

 

his such act shall also be the same offence.

 

(3) Any person alleged to have committed the offence mentioned in this article shall be sentenced with the highest punishment prescribed for other offences by the existing laws.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.7B.title: Basic provisions of the Constitution are not amendable

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Basic provisions of the Constitution are not amendable: 7B.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding basic provisions of the constitution are not amendable.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.7B.full_text: 7B. Notwithstanding anything contained in article 142 of the Constitution, the preamble, all articles of Part I, all articles of Part II, subject to the provisions of Part IXA all articles of Part III, and the provisions of articles relating to the basic structures of the Constitution including article 150 of Part XI shall not be amendable by way of insertion, modification, substitution, repeal or by any other means.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.8.title: Fundamental principles

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Fundamental principles: 8.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding fundamental principles.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.8.full_text:
8. (1) The principles of nationalism, socialism, democracy and secularism, together with the principles derived from those as set out in this Part, shall constitute the fundamental principles of state policy.
(2) The principles set out in this Part shall be fundamental to the governance of Bangladesh, shall be applied by the State in the making of laws, shall be a guide to the interpretation of the Constitution and of the other laws of Bangladesh, and shall form the basis of the work of the State and of its citizens, but shall not be judicially enforceable.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.9.title: Nationalism

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Nationalism: 9.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding nationalism.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.9.full_text: 9. The unity and solidarity of the Bangalee nation, which, deriving its identity from its language and culture, attained sovereign and independent Bangladesh through a united and determined struggle in the war of independence, shall be the basis of Bangalee nationalism.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.10.title: Socialism and freedom from exploitation

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Socialism and freedom from exploitation: 10.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding socialism and freedom from exploitation.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.10.full_text: 10. A socialist economic system shall be established with a view to ensuring the attainment of a just and egalitarian society, free from the exploitation of man by man.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.11.title: Democracy and human rights

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Democracy and human rights: 11.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding democracy and human rights.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.11.full_text:
11. The Republic shall be a democracy in which fundamental human rights and freedoms and respect for the dignity and worth of the human person shall be guaranteed  , and in which effective participation by the
people through their elected representatives in administration at all levels shall be ensured.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.12.title: Secularism and freedom of religion

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Secularism and freedom of religion: 12.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding secularism and freedom of religion.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.13.title: Principles of ownership

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Principles of ownership: 13.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding principles of ownership.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.13.full_text:
13. The people shall own or control the instruments and means of production and distribution, and with this end in view ownership shall assume the following forms –
(a) state ownership, that is ownership by the State on behalf of the people through the creation of an efficient and dynamic nationalised public sector embracing the key sectors of the economy;
(b) co operative ownership, that is ownership by co operatives on behalf of their members within such limits as may be prescribed by law; and
(c) private ownership, that is ownership by individuals within such limits as may be prescribed by law.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.14.title: Emancipation of peasants and workers

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Emancipation of peasants and workers: 14.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding emancipation of peasants and workers.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.14.full_text: 14. It shall be a fundamental responsibility of the State to emancipate the toiling masses the peasants and workers and backward sections of the people from all forms of exploitation.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.15.title: Provision of basic necessities

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Provision of basic necessities: 15.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding provision of basic necessities.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.16.title: Rural development and agricultural revolution

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Rural development and agricultural revolution: 16.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding rural development and agricultural revolution.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.16.full_text: 16. The State shall adopt effective measures to bring about a radical transformation in the rural areas through the promotion of an agricultural revolution, the provision of rural electrification, the development of cottage and other industries, and the improvement of education, communications and public health, in those areas, so as progressively to remove the disparity in the standards of living between the urban and the rural areas.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.17.title: Free and compulsory education

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Free and compulsory education: 17.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding free and compulsory education.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.18.title: Public health and morality

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Public health and morality: 18.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding public health and morality.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.18.full_text:
18. (1) The State shall regard the raising of the level of nutrition and the improvement of public health as among its primary duties, and in particular shall adopt effective measures to prevent the consumption, except for medical purposes or for such other purposes as may be prescribed by law, of alcoholic and other intoxicating drinks and of drugs which are injurious to health.
(2) The State shall adopt effective measures to prevent prostitution and gambling.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.18A.title: Protection and improvement of environment and biodiversity

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Protection and improvement of environment and biodiversity: 18A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding protection and improvement of environment and biodiversity.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.18A.full_text: 18A. The State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment and to preserve and safeguard the natural resources, bio-diversity, wetlands, forests and wild life for the present and future citizens.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.19.title: Equality of opportunity

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Equality of opportunity: 19.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding equality of opportunity.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.19.full_text:
19. (1) The State shall endeavour to ensure equality of opportunity to all citizens.
(2) The State shall adopt effective measures to remove social and economic inequality between man and man and to ensure the equitable distribution of wealth among citizens, and of opportunities in order to attain a uniform level of economic development throughout the Republic.
(3)The State Shall endeavour to ensure equality of opportunity and participation of women in all spheres of national life.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.20.title: Work as a right and duty

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Work as a right and duty: 20.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding work as a right and duty.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.20.full_text:
20. (1) Work is a right, a duty and a matter of honour for every citizen who is capable of working, and everyone shall be paid for his work on the basis of the principle “from each according to his abilities, to each according to his work”.
(2) The State shall endeavour to create conditions in which, as a general principle, persons shall not be able to enjoy unearned incomes, and in which human labour in every form, intellectual and physical, shall become a fuller expression of creative endeavour and of the human personality.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.21.title: Duties of citizens and of public servants

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Duties of citizens and of public servants: 21.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding duties of citizens and of public servants.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.21.full_text:
21. (1) It is the duty of every citizen to observe the Constitution and the laws, to maintain discipline, to perform public duties and to protect public property.
(2) Every person in the service of the Republic has a duty to strive at all times to serve the people.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.22.title: Separation of Judiciary from the executive

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Separation of Judiciary from the executive: 22.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding separation of judiciary from the executive.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.22.full_text: 22. The State shall ensure the separation of the judiciary from the executive organs of the State.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.23.title: National culture

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - National culture: 23.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding national culture.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.23.full_text: 23. The State shall adopt measures to conserve the cultural traditions and heritage of the people, and so to foster and improve the national language, literature and the arts that all sections of the people are afforded the opportunity to contribute towards and to participate in the enrichment of the national culture.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.23A.title: The culture of tribes, minor races, ethnic sects and communities

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - The culture of tribes, minor races, ethnic sects and communities: 23A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding the culture of tribes, minor races, ethnic sects and communities.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.23A.full_text: 23A. The State shall take steps to protect and develop the unique local culture and tradition of the tribes, minor races, ethnic sects and communities.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.24.title: National monuments, etc.

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - National monuments, etc.: 24.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding national monuments, etc..
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.24.full_text: 24. The State shall adopt measures for the protection against disfigurement, damage or removal of all monuments, objects or places of special artistic or historic importance or interest.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.25.title: Promotion of international peace, security and solidarity

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Promotion of international peace, security and solidarity: 25.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding promotion of international peace, security and solidarity.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.25.full_text:
25.  The State shall base its international relations on the principles of respect for national sovereignty and equality, non interference in the internal affairs of other countries, peaceful settlement of international disputes, and respect for
international law and the principles enunciated in the United Nations Charter, and on the basis of those principles shall –
(a) strive for the renunciation of the use of force in international relations and for general and complete disarmament;
(b) uphold the right of every people freely to determine and build up its own social, economic and political system by ways and means of its own free choice; and
(c) support oppressed peoples throughout the world waging a just struggle against imperialism, colonialism or racialism.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.26.title: Laws inconsistent with fundamental rights to be void

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Laws inconsistent with fundamental rights to be void: 26.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding laws inconsistent with fundamental rights to be void.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.26.full_text:
26. (1) All existing law inconsistent with the provisions of this Part shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, become void on the commencement of this Constitution.
(2) The State shall not make any law inconsistent with any provisions of this Part, and any law so made shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, be void.
(3) Nothing in this article shall apply to any amendment of this Constitution made under article 142.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.27.title: Equality before law

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Equality before law: 27.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding equality before law.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.27.full_text: 27. All citizens are equal before law and are entitled to equal protection of law.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.28.title: Discrimination on grounds of religion, etc.

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Discrimination on grounds of religion, etc.: 28.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding discrimination on grounds of religion, etc..
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.28.full_text:
28. (1) The State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
(2) Women shall have equal rights with men in all spheres of the State and of public life.
(3) No citizen shall, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth be subjected to any disability, liability, restriction or condition with regard to access to any place of public entertainment or resort, or admission to any educational institution.
(4) Nothing in this article shall prevent the State from making special provision in favour of women or children or for the advancement of any backward section of citizens.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.29.title: Equality of opportunity in public employment

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Equality of opportunity in public employment: 29.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding equality of opportunity in public employment.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.30.title: Prohibition of foreign titles, etc.

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Prohibition of foreign titles, etc.: 30.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding prohibition of foreign titles, etc..
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.30.full_text: 30. No citizen shall, without the prior approval of the President, accept any title, honour, award or decoration from any foreign state.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.31.title: Right to protection of law

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Right to protection of law: 31.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding right to protection of law.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.31.full_text: 31. To enjoy the protection of the law, and to be treated in accordance with law, and only in accordance with law, is the inalienable right of every citizen, wherever he may be, and of every other person for the time being within Bangladesh, and in particular no action detrimental to the life, liberty, body, reputation or property of any person shall be taken except in accordance with law.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.32.title: Protection of right to life and personal liberty

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Protection of right to life and personal liberty: 32.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding protection of right to life and personal liberty.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.32.full_text: 32. No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty save in accordance with law.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.33.title: Safeguards as to arrest and detention

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Safeguards as to arrest and detention: 33.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding safeguards as to arrest and detention.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.33.full_text:
33. (1) No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest, nor shall he be denied the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of his choice.
(2) Every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of twenty four hours of such arrest, excluding the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the Court of the magistrate, and no such person shall be detained in custody beyond the said period without the authority of a magistrate.
(3) Nothing in clauses (1) and (2) shall apply to any person–
(a) who for the time being is an enemy alien; or
(b) who is arrested or detained under any law providing for preventive detention.
(4) No law providing for preventive detention shall authorise the detention of a person for a period exceeding six months unless an Advisory Board consisting of three persons, of whom two shall be persons who are, or have been, or are qualified to be appointed as, Judges of the Supreme Court and the other shall be a person who is a senior officer in the service of the Republic, has, after affording him an opportunity of being heard in person, reported before the expiration of the said period of six months that there is, in its opinion, sufficient cause for such detention.
(5) When any person is detained in pursuance of an order made under any law providing for preventive detention, the authority making the order shall, as soon as may be, communicate to such person the grounds on which the order has been made, and shall afford him the earliest opportunity of making a representation against the order:
Provided that the authority making any such order may refuse to disclose facts which such authority considers to be against the public interest to disclose.
(6) Parliament may by law prescribe the procedure to be followed by an Advisory Board in an inquiry under clause (4).

BD-CONST-1972:Art.34.title: Prohibition of forced labour

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Prohibition of forced labour: 34.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding prohibition of forced labour.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.34.full_text:
34. (1) All forms of forced labour are prohibited and any contravention of this provision shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.
(2) Nothing in this article shall apply to compulsory labour–
(a) by persons undergoing lawful punishment for a criminal offence; or
(b) required by any law for public purposes.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.35.title: Protection in respect of trial and punishment

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Protection in respect of trial and punishment: 35.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding protection in respect of trial and punishment.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.35.full_text:
35. (1) No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offence, nor be subjected to a penalty greater than, or different from, that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence.
(2) No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.
(3) Every person accused of a criminal offence shall have the right to a speedy and public trial by an independent and impartial Court or tribunal established by law.
(4) No person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.
(5) No person shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman, or degrading punishment or treatment.
(6) Nothing in clause (3) or clause (5) shall affect the operation of any existing law which prescribes any punishment or procedure for trial.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.36.title: Freedom of movement

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Freedom of movement: 36.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding freedom of movement.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.36.full_text: 36. Subject to any reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the public interest, every citizen shall have the right to move freely throughout Bangladesh, to reside and settle in any place therein and to leave and re-enter Bangladesh.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.37.title: Freedom of assembly

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Freedom of assembly: 37.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding freedom of assembly.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.37.full_text: 37. Every citizen shall have the right to assemble and to participate in public meetings and processions peacefully and without arms, subject to any reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interests of public order or public health.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.38.title: Freedom of association

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Freedom of association: 38.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding freedom of association.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.39.title: Freedom of thought and conscience, and of speech

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Freedom of thought and conscience, and of speech: 39.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding freedom of thought and conscience, and of speech.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.39.full_text:
39. (1) Freedom of thought and conscience is guaranteed.
(2) Subject to any reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interests of the security of the State, friendly relations with foreign states, public order, decency or morality, or in relation to contempt of court, defamation or incitement to an offence–
(a) the right of every citizen to freedom of speech and expression; and
(b) freedom of the press,
are guaranteed.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.40.title: Freedom of profession or occupation

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Freedom of profession or occupation: 40.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding freedom of profession or occupation.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.40.full_text: 40. Subject to any restrictions imposed by law, every citizen possessing such qualifications, if any, as may be prescribed by law in relation to his profession, occupation, trade or business shall have the right to enter upon any lawful profession or occupation, and to conduct any lawful trade or business.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.41.title: Freedom of religion

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Freedom of religion: 41.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding freedom of religion.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.41.full_text:
41. (1) Subject to law, public order and morality –
(a) every citizen has the right to profess, practise or propagate any religion;
(b) every religious community or denomination has the right to establish, maintain and manage its religious institutions.
(2) No person attending any educational institution shall be required to receive religious instruction, or to take part in or to attend any religious ceremony or worship, if that instruction, ceremony or worship relates to a religion other than his own.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.42.title: Rights to property

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Rights to property: 42.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding rights to property.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.42.full_text:
42. (1) Subject to any restrictions imposed by law, every citizen shall have the right to acquire, hold, transfer or otherwise dispose of property, and no property shall be compulsorily acquired, nationalised or requisitioned save by authority of law.
(2) A law made under clause (1) of this article shall provide for the acquisition, nationalisation or requisition with compensation and shall fix the amount of compensation or specify the principles on which, and the manner in which, the compensation is to be assessed and paid ; but no such law shall be called in question in any court on the ground that any provision of the law in respect of such compensation is not adequate.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.43.title: Protection of home and correspondence

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Protection of home and correspondence: 43.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding protection of home and correspondence.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.43.full_text:
43. Every citizen shall have the right, subject to any reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interests of the security of the State, public order, public morality or public health –
(a) to be secured in his home against entry, search and seizure; and
(b) to the privacy of his correspondence and other means of communication.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.44.title: Enforcement of fundamental rights

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Enforcement of fundamental rights: 44.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding enforcement of fundamental rights.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.44.full_text:
44. (1) The right to move the High Court Division in accordance with clause (1) of article 102, for the enforcement of the rights conferred by this Part is guaranteed.
(2) Without prejudice to the powers of the High Court Division under article 102, Parliament may by law empower any other court, within the local limits of its jurisdiction, to exercise all or any of those powers.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.45.title: Modification of rights in respect of disciplinary law

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Modification of rights in respect of disciplinary law: 45.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding modification of rights in respect of disciplinary law.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.45.full_text: 45. Nothing in this Part shall apply to any provision of a disciplinary law relating to members of a disciplined force, being a provision limited to the purpose of ensuring the proper discharge of their duties or the maintenance of discipline in that force.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.46.title: Power to provide indemnity

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Power to provide indemnity: 46.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding power to provide indemnity.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.46.full_text: 46. Notwithstanding anything in the foregoing provisions of this Part, Parliament may by law make provision for indemnifying any person in the service of the Republic or any other person in respect of any act done by him in connection with the national liberation struggle or the maintenance or restoration of order in any area in Bangladesh or validate any sentence passed, punishment inflicted, forfeiture ordered, or other act done in any such area.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.47.title: Saving for certain laws

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Saving for certain laws: 47.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding saving for certain laws.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.47A.title: Inapplicability of certain articles

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Inapplicability of certain articles: 47A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding inapplicability of certain articles.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.47A.full_text:
47A. (1) The rights guaranteed under article 31, clauses (1) and (3) of article 35 and article 44 shall not apply to any person to whom a law specified in clause (3) of article 47 applies.
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Constitution, no person to whom a law specified in clause (3) of article 47 applies shall have the right to move the Supreme Court for any of the remedies under this Constitution.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.48.title: The President

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - The President: 48.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding the president.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.48.full_text:
48. (1) There shall be a President of Bangladesh who shall be elected by members of Parliament in accordance with law.
(2) The President shall, as Head of State, take precedence over all other persons in the State, and shall exercise the powers and perform the duties conferred and imposed on him by this Constitution and by any other law.
(3) In the exercise of all his functions, save only that of appointing the Prime Minister pursuant to clause (3) of article 56 and the Chief Justice pursuant to clause (1) of article 95, the President shall act in accordance with the advice of the Prime Minister:
Provided that the question whether any, and if so what, advice has been tendered by the Prime Minister to the President shall not be enquired into in any court.
(4) A person shall not be qualified for election as President if he –
(a) is less than thirty five years of age; or
(b) is not qualified for election as a member of Parliament; or
(c) has been removed from the office of President by impeachment under this Constitution.
(5) The Prime Minister shall keep the President informed on matters of domestic and foreign policy, and submit for the consideration of the Cabinet any matter which the President may request him to refer to it.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.49.title: Prerogative of mercy

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Prerogative of mercy: 49.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding prerogative of mercy.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.49.full_text: 49. The President shall have power to grant pardons, reprieves and respites and to remit, suspend or commute any sentence passed by any court, tribunal or other authority.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.50.title: Term of office of President

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Term of office of President: 50.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding term of office of president.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.50.full_text:
50. (1) Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, the President shall hold office for a term of five years form the date on which he enters upon his office:
Provided that notwithstanding the expiration of his term the President shall continue to hold office until his successor enters upon office.
(2) No person shall hold office as President for more than two terms, whether or not the terms are consecutive.
(3) The President may resign his office by writing under his hand addressed to the Speaker.
(4) The President during his term of office shall not be qualified for election as a member of Parliament, and if a member of Parliament is elected as President he shall vacate his seat in Parliament on the day on which he enters upon his office as President.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.51.title: President's immunity

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - President's immunity: 51.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding president's immunity.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.51.full_text:
51. (1) Without prejudice to the provisions of article 52, the President shall not be answerable in any court for anything done or omitted by him in the exercise or purported exercise of the functions of his office, but this clause shall not prejudice the right of any person to take proceedings against the Government.
(2) During his term of office no criminal proceedings whatsoever shall be instituted or continued against the President in, and no process for his arrest or imprisonment shall issue from, any court.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.52.title: Impeachment of the President

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Impeachment of the President: 52.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding impeachment of the president.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.52.full_text:
52. (1) The President may be impeached on a charge of violating this Constitution or of grave misconduct, preferred by a notice of motion signed by a majority of the total number of members of Parliament and delivered to the Speaker, setting
out the particulars of the charge, and the motion shall not be debated earlier than fourteen nor later than thirty days after the notice is so delivered; and the Speaker shall forthwith summon Parliament if it is not in session.
(2) The conduct of the President may be referred by Parliament to any court, tribunal or body appointed or designated by Parliament for the investigation of charge under this article.
(3) The President shall have the right to appear and to be represented during the consideration of the charge.
(4) If after the consideration of the charge a resolution is passed by Parliament by the votes of not less than two thirds of the total number of members declaring that the charge has been substantiated, the President shall vacate his office on the date on which the resolution is passed.
(5) Where the Speaker is exercising the functions of the President under article 54 the provisions of this article shall apply subject to the modifications that the reference to the Speaker in clause (1) shall be construed as a reference to the Deputy Speaker, and that the reference in clause (4) to the vacation by the President of his office shall be construed as a reference to the vacation by the Speaker of his office as Speaker; and on the passing of a resolution such as is referred to in clause (4) the Speaker shall cease to exercise the functions of President.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.53.title: Removal of President on ground of incapacity

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Removal of President on ground of incapacity: 53.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding removal of president on ground of incapacity.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.53.full_text:
53. (1) The President may be removed from office on the ground of physical or mental incapacity on a motion of which notice, signed by a majority of the total number of members of Parliament, is delivered to the Speaker, setting out particulars of the alleged incapacity.
(2) On receipt of the notice the Speaker shall forthwith summon Parliament if it is not in session and shall call for a resolution constituting a medical board (hereinafter in this article called “the Board”), and upon the necessary motion being made and carried shall forthwith cause a copy of the
notice to be transmitted to the President together with a request signed by the Speaker that the President submit himself within a period of ten days from the date of the request to an examination by the Board.
(3) The motion for removal shall not be put to the vote earlier than fourteen nor later than thirty days after notice of the motion is delivered to the Speaker, and if it is again necessary to summon Parliament in order to enable the motion to be made within that period, the Speaker shall summon Parliament.
(4) The President shall have the right to appear and to be represented during the consideration of the motion.
(5) If the President has not submitted himself to an examination by the Board before the motion is made in Parliament, the motion may be put to the vote, and if it is passed by the votes of not less than two thirds of the total number of members of Parliament, the President shall vacate his office on the date on which the motion is passed.
(6) If before the motion for removal is made in Parliament, the President has submitted himself to an examination by the Board, the motion shall not be put to the vote until the Board has been given an opportunity of reporting its opinion to Parliament.
(7) If after consideration by Parliament of the motion and of the report of the Board (which shall be submitted within seven days of the examination held pursuant to clause (2) and if not so submitted shall be dispensed with) the motion is passed by the votes of not less than two thirds of the total number of members of Parliament, the President shall vacate his office on the date on which the resolution is passed.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.54.title: Speaker to act as President during absence, etc.

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Speaker to act as President during absence, etc.: 54.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding speaker to act as president during absence, etc..
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.54.full_text: 54. If a vacancy occurs in the office of President or if the President is unable to discharge the functions of his office on account of absence, illness or any other cause the Speaker shall discharge those functions until a President is elected or until the President resumes the functions of his office, as the case may be.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.55.title: The Cabinet

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - The Cabinet: 55.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding the cabinet.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.55.full_text:
55. (1) There shall be a Cabinet for Bangladesh having the Prime Minister at its head and comprising also such other Ministers as the Prime Minister may from time to time designate.
(2) The executive power of the Republic shall, in accordance with this Constitution, be exercised by or on the authority of the Prime Minister.
(3) The Cabinet shall be collectively responsible to Parliament.
(4) All executive actions of the Government shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President.
(5) The President shall by rules specify the manner in which orders and other instruments made in his name shall be attested or authenticated, and the validity of any order or instrument so attested or authenticated shall not be questioned in any court on the ground that it was not duly made or executed.
(6) The President shall make rules for the allocation and transaction of the business of the Government.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.56.title: Ministers

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Ministers: 56.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding ministers.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.56.full_text:
56. (1) There shall be a Prime Minister, and such other Ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers as may be determined by the Prime Minister.
(2) The appointments of the Prime Minister and other Ministers and of the Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers, shall be made by the President:
Provided that not less than nine tenths of their number shall be appointed from among members of Parliament and not more than one tenth of their number may be chosen from among persons qualified for election as members of Parliament.
(3) The President shall appoint as Prime Minister the member of Parliament who appears to him to command the support of the majority of the members of Parliament.
(4) If occasion arises for making any appointment under clause (2) or clause (3) between a dissolution of Parliament and the next following general election of members of Parliament, the persons who were such members immediately before the dissolution shall be regarded for the purpose of this clause as continuing to be such members.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.57.title: Tenure of office of Prime Minister

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Tenure of office of Prime Minister: 57.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding tenure of office of prime minister.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.57.full_text:
57. (1) The office of the Prime Minister shall become vacant–
(a) if he resigns from office at any time by placing his resignation in the hands of the President; or
(b) if he ceases to be a member of Parliament.
(2) If the Prime Minister ceases to retain the support of a majority of the members of Parliament, he shall either resign his office or advise the President in writing to dissolve Parliament, and if he so advises the President shall, if he is satisfied that no other member of Parliament commands the support of the majority of the members of Parliament, dissolve Parliament accordingly.
(3) Nothing in this article shall disqualify Prime Minister for holding office until his successor has entered upon office.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.58.title: Tenure of office of other Ministers

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Tenure of office of other Ministers: 58.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding tenure of office of other ministers.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.58.full_text:
58. (1) The office of a Minister other than the Prime Minister shall become vacant –
(a) if he resigns from office by placing his resignation in the hands of the Prime Minister for submission to the President;
(b) if he ceases to be a member of Parliament, but this shall not be applicable to a Minister chosen under the proviso to article 56(2);
(c) if the President, pursuant to the provisions of clause (2), so directs; or
(d) as provided in clause (4).
(2) The Prime Minister may at any time request a Minister to resign, and if such Minister fails to comply with the request, may advise the President to terminate the appointment of such Minister.
(3) Nothing in sub clauses (a), (b) and (d) of clause (1) shall disqualify a Minister for holding office during any period in which Parliament stands dissolved.
(4) If the Prime Minister resigns from or ceases to hold office each of the other Ministers shall be deemed also to have resigned from office but shall, subject to the provisions of this Chapter, continue to hold office until his successor has entered upon office.
(5) In this article “Minister” includes Minister of State and Deputy Minister.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.59.title: Local government

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Local government: 59.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding local government.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.60.title: Powers of local government bodies

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Powers of local government bodies: 60.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding powers of local government bodies.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.60.full_text: 60. For the purpose of giving full effect to the provisions of article 59 Parliament shall, by law, confer powers on the local government bodies referred to in that article, including power to impose taxes for local purposes, to prepare their budgets and to maintain funds.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.61.title: Supreme command

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Supreme command: 61.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding supreme command.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.61.full_text: 61. The supreme command of the defence services of Bangladesh shall vest in the President and the exercise thereof shall be regulated by law.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.62.title: Recruitment, etc., of defence services

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - Recruitment, etc., of defence services: 62.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding recruitment, etc., of defence services.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.63.title: War

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - War: 63.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding war.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.63.full_text: 63. (1) War shall not be declared and the Republic shall not participate in any war except with the assent of Parliament.

BD-CONST-1972:Art.64.title: The Attorney-General

summary.one_week_summary: Constitution of Bangladesh - The Attorney-General: 64.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Constitution of Bangladesh regarding the attorney-general.
