US-9-USC-2.full_text: A written provision in any maritime transaction or a contract evidencing a transaction involving commerce to settle by arbitration a controversy thereafter arising out of such contract or transaction, or the refusal to perform the whole or any part thereof, or an agreement in writing to submit to arbitration an existing controversy arising out of such a contract, transaction, or refusal, shall be valid, irrevocable, and enforceable, save upon such grounds as exist at law or in equity for the revocation of any contract or as otherwise provided in chapter 4.

US-9-USC-3.title: 9 U.S.C. § 3 - Stay of proceedings where issue therein referable to arbitration

summary.one_week_summary: 9 U.S.C. - Stay of proceedings where issue therein referable to arbitration: If any suit or proceeding be brought in any of the courts of the United States upon any issue referable to arbitration under an agreement in writing for such arbitration, the court in which such suit is pending, upon being satisfied that the issue involved in such suit or proceeding is referable to arbitration under such an agreement, shall on application of one of the parties stay the trial of the action until such arbitration has been had in accordance with the terms of the agreement, providing the applicant for the stay is not in default in proceeding with such arbitration.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under 9 U.S.C. regarding stay of proceedings where issue therein referable to arbitration.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

US-9-USC-3.full_text: If any suit or proceeding be brought in any of the courts of the United States upon any issue referable to arbitration under an agreement in writing for such arbitration, the court in which such suit is pending, upon being satisfied that the issue involved in such suit or proceeding is referable to arbitration under such an agreement, shall on application of one of the parties stay the trial of the action until such arbitration has been had in accordance with the terms of the agreement, providing the applicant for the stay is not in default in proceeding with such arbitration.

US-9-USC-4.title: 9 U.S.C. § 4 - Failure to arbitrate under agreement; petition to United States court having jurisdiction for order to compel arbitration; notice and service thereof; hearing and determination

summary.one_week_summary: 9 U.S.C. - Failure to arbitrate under agreement; petition to United States court having jurisdiction for order to compel arbitration; notice and service thereof; hearing and determination: A party aggrieved by the alleged failure, neglect, or refusal of another to arbitrate under a written agreement for arbitration may petition any United States district court which, save for such agreement, would have jurisdiction under title 28, in a civil action or in admiralty of the subject matter of a suit arising out of the controversy between the parties, for an order directing that such arbitration proceed in the manner provided for in such agreement.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under 9 U.S.C. regarding failure to arbitrate under agreement; petition to united states court having jurisdiction for order to compel arbitration; notice and service thereof; hearing and determination.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

US-9-USC-4.full_text: A party aggrieved by the alleged failure, neglect, or refusal of another to arbitrate under a written agreement for arbitration may petition any United States district court which, save for such agreement, would have jurisdiction under title 28, in a civil action or in admiralty of the subject matter of a suit arising out of the controversy between the parties, for an order directing that such arbitration proceed in the manner provided for in such agreement. Five days’ notice in writing of such application shall be served upon the party in default. Service thereof shall be made in the manner provided by the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure. The court shall hear the parties, and upon being satisfied that the making of the agreement for arbitration or the failure to comply therewith is not in issue, the court shall make an order directing the parties to proceed to arbitration in accordance with the terms of the agreement. The hearing and proceedings, under such agreement, shall be within the district in which the petition for an order directing such arbitration is filed. If the making of the arbitration agreement or the failure, neglect, or refusal to perform the same be in issue, the court shall proceed summarily to the trial thereof. If no jury trial be demanded by the party alleged to be in default, or if the matter in dispute is within admiralty jurisdiction, the court shall hear and determine such issue. Where such an issue is raised, the party alleged to be in default may, except in cases of admiralty, on or before the return day of the notice of application, demand a jury trial of such issue, and upon such demand the court shall make an order referring the issue or issues to a jury in the manner provided by the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, or may specially call a jury for that purpose. If the jury find that no agreement in writing for arbitration was made or that there is no default in proceeding thereunder, the proceeding shall be dismissed. If the jury find that an agreement for arbitration was made in writing and that there is a default in proceeding thereunder, the court shall make an order summarily directing the parties to proceed with the arbitration in accordance with the terms thereof.

US-9-USC-5.title: 9 U.S.C. § 5 - Appointment of arbitrators or umpire

summary.one_week_summary: 9 U.S.C. - Appointment of arbitrators or umpire: If in the agreement provision be made for a method of naming or appointing an arbitrator or arbitrators or an umpire, such method shall be followed; but if no method be provided therein, or if a method be provided and any party thereto shall fail to avail himself of such method, or if for any other reason there shall be a lapse in the naming of an arbitrator or arbitrators or umpire, or in filling a vacancy, then upon the application of either party to the controversy the court shall designate and appoint an arbitrator or arbitrators or umpire, as the case may require, who shall act under the said agreement with the same force and effect as if he or they had been specifically named therein; and unless otherwise provided in the agreement the arbitration shall be by a single arbitrator.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under 9 U.S.C. regarding appointment of arbitrators or umpire.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

US-9-USC-5.full_text: If in the agreement provision be made for a method of naming or appointing an arbitrator or arbitrators or an umpire, such method shall be followed; but if no method be provided therein, or if a method be provided and any party thereto shall fail to avail himself of such method, or if for any other reason there shall be a lapse in the naming of an arbitrator or arbitrators or umpire, or in filling a vacancy, then upon the application of either party to the controversy the court shall designate and appoint an arbitrator or arbitrators or umpire, as the case may require, who shall act under the said agreement with the same force and effect as if he or they had been specifically named therein; and unless otherwise provided in the agreement the arbitration shall be by a single arbitrator.

US-9-USC-6.title: 9 U.S.C. § 6 - Application heard as motion

summary.one_week_summary: 9 U.S.C. - Application heard as motion: Any application to the court hereunder shall be made and heard in the manner provided by law for the making and hearing of motions, except as otherwise herein expressly provided.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under 9 U.S.C. regarding application heard as motion.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

US-9-USC-6.full_text: Any application to the court hereunder shall be made and heard in the manner provided by law for the making and hearing of motions, except as otherwise herein expressly provided.

US-9-USC-7.title: 9 U.S.C. § 7 - Witnesses before arbitrators; fees; compelling attendance

summary.one_week_summary: 9 U.S.C. - Witnesses before arbitrators; fees; compelling attendance: The arbitrators selected either as prescribed in this title or otherwise, or a majority of them, may summon in writing any person to attend before them or any of them as a witness and in a proper case to bring with him or them any book, record, document, or paper which may be deemed material as evidence in the case.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under 9 U.S.C. regarding witnesses before arbitrators; fees; compelling attendance.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

US-9-USC-7.full_text: The arbitrators selected either as prescribed in this title or otherwise, or a majority of them, may summon in writing any person to attend before them or any of them as a witness and in a proper case to bring with him or them any book, record, document, or paper which may be deemed material as evidence in the case. The fees for such attendance shall be the same as the fees of witnesses before masters of the United States courts. Said summons shall issue in the name of the arbitrator or arbitrators, or a majority of them, and shall be signed by the arbitrators, or a majority of them, and shall be directed to the said person and shall be served in the same manner as subpoenas to appear and testify before the court; if any person or persons so summoned to testify shall refuse or neglect to obey said summons, upon petition the United States district court for the district in which such arbitrators, or a majority of them, are sitting may compel the attendance of such person or persons before said arbitrator or arbitrators, or punish said person or persons for contempt in the same manner provided by law for securing the attendance of witnesses or their punishment for neglect or refusal to attend in the courts of the United States.

US-9-USC-8.title: 9 U.S.C. § 8 - Proceedings begun by libel in admiralty and seizure of vessel or property

summary.one_week_summary: 9 U.S.C. - Proceedings begun by libel in admiralty and seizure of vessel or property: If the basis of jurisdiction be a cause of action otherwise justiciable in admiralty, then, notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, the party claiming to be aggrieved may begin his proceeding hereunder by libel and seizure of the vessel or other property of the other party according to the usual course of admiralty proceedings, and the court shall then have jurisdiction to direct the parties to proceed with the arbitration and shall retain jurisdiction to enter its decree upon the award.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under 9 U.S.C. regarding proceedings begun by libel in admiralty and seizure of vessel or property.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

US-9-USC-8.full_text: If the basis of jurisdiction be a cause of action otherwise justiciable in admiralty, then, notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, the party claiming to be aggrieved may begin his proceeding hereunder by libel and seizure of the vessel or other property of the other party according to the usual course of admiralty proceedings, and the court shall then have jurisdiction to direct the parties to proceed with the arbitration and shall retain jurisdiction to enter its decree upon the award.

US-9-USC-9.title: 9 U.S.C. § 9 - Award of arbitrators; confirmation; jurisdiction; procedure

summary.one_week_summary: 9 U.S.C. - Award of arbitrators; confirmation; jurisdiction; procedure: If the parties in their agreement have agreed that a judgment of the court shall be entered upon the award made pursuant to the arbitration, and shall specify the court, then at any time within one year after the award is made any party to the arbitration may apply to the court so specified for an order confirming the award, and thereupon the court must grant such an order unless the award is vacated, modified, or corrected as prescribed in sections 10 and 11 of this title.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under 9 U.S.C. regarding award of arbitrators; confirmation; jurisdiction; procedure.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

US-9-USC-9.full_text: If the parties in their agreement have agreed that a judgment of the court shall be entered upon the award made pursuant to the arbitration, and shall specify the court, then at any time within one year after the award is made any party to the arbitration may apply to the court so specified for an order confirming the award, and thereupon the court must grant such an order unless the award is vacated, modified, or corrected as prescribed in sections 10 and 11 of this title. If no court is specified in the agreement of the parties, then such application may be made to the United States court in and for the district within which such award was made. Notice of the application shall be served upon the adverse party, and thereupon the court shall have jurisdiction of such party as though he had appeared generally in the proceeding. If the adverse party is a resident of the district within which the award was made, such service shall be made upon the adverse party or his attorney as prescribed by law for service of notice of motion in an action in the same court. US-15-USC-8.title: 15 U.S.C. § 8 - Trusts in restraint of import trade illegal; penalty

summary.one_week_summary: 15 U.S.C. - Trusts in restraint of import trade illegal; penalty: Every combination, conspiracy, trust, agreement, or contract is declared to be contrary to public policy, illegal, and void when the same is made by or between two or more persons or corporations, either of whom, as agent or principal, is engaged in importing any article from any foreign country into the United States, and when such combination, conspiracy, trust, agreement, or contract is intended to operate in restraint of lawful trade, or free competition in lawful trade or commerce, or to increase the market price in any part of the United States of any article or articles imported or intended to be imported into the United States, or of any manufacture into which such imported article enters or is intended to enter.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under 15 U.S.C. regarding trusts in restraint of import trade illegal; penalty.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

US-15-USC-8.full_text: Every combination, conspiracy, trust, agreement, or contract is declared to be contrary to public policy, illegal, and void when the same is made by or between two or more persons or corporations, either of whom, as agent or principal, is engaged in importing any article from any foreign country into the United States, and when such combination, conspiracy, trust, agreement, or contract is intended to operate in restraint of lawful trade, or free competition in lawful trade or commerce, or to increase the market price in any part of the United States of any article or articles imported or intended to be imported into the United States, or of any manufacture into which such imported article enters or is intended to enter. Every person who shall be engaged in the importation of goods or any commodity from any foreign country in violation of this section, or who shall combine or conspire with another to violate the same, is guilty of a misdemeanor, and on conviction thereof in any court of the United States such person shall be fined in a sum not less than $100 and not exceeding $5,000, and shall be further punished by imprisonment, in the discretion of the court, for a term not less than three months nor exceeding twelve months.

US-15-USC-18.full_text: No person engaged in commerce or in any activity affecting commerce shall acquire, directly or indirectly, the whole or any part of the stock or other share capital and no person subject to the jurisdiction of the Federal Trade Commission shall acquire the whole or any part of the assets of another person engaged also in commerce or in any activity affecting commerce, where in any line of commerce or in any activity affecting commerce in any section of the country, the effect of such acquisition may be substantially to lessen competition, or to tend to create a monopoly.No person shall acquire, directly or indirectly, the whole or any part of the stock or other share capital and no person subject to the jurisdiction of the Federal Trade Commission shall acquire the whole or any part of the assets of one or more persons engaged in commerce or in any activity affecting commerce, where in any line of commerce or in any activity affecting commerce in any section of the country, the effect of such acquisition, of such stocks or assets, or of the use of such stock by the voting or granting of proxies or otherwise, may be substantially to lessen competition, or to tend to create a monopoly.This section shall not apply to persons purchasing such stock solely for investment and not using the same by voting or otherwise to bring about, or in attempting to bring about, the substantial lessening of competition. Nor shall anything contained in this section prevent a corporation engaged in commerce or in any activity affecting commerce from causing the formation of subsidiary corporations for the actual carrying on of their immediate lawful business, or the natural and legitimate branches or extensions thereof, or from owning and holding all or a part of the stock of such subsidiary corporations, when the effect of such formation is not to substantially lessen competition.Nor shall anything herein contained be construed to prohibit any common carrier subject to the laws to regulate commerce from aiding in the construction of branches or short lines so located as to become feeders to the main line of the company so aiding in such construction or from acquiring or owning all or any part of the stock of such branch lines, nor to prevent any such common carrier from acquiring and owning all or any part of the stock of a branch or short line constructed by an independent company where there is no substantial competition between the company owning the branch line so constructed and the company owning the main line acquiring the property or an interest therein, nor to prevent such common carrier from extending any of its lines through the medium of the acquisition of stock or otherwise of any other common carrier where there is no substantial competition between the company extending its lines and the company whose stock, property, or an interest therein is so acquired.Nothing contained in this section shall be held to affect or impair any right heretofore legally acquired: , That nothing in this section shall be held or construed to authorize or make lawful anything heretofore prohibited or made illegal by the antitrust laws, nor to exempt any person from the penal provisions thereof or the civil remedies therein provided.ProvidedNothing contained in this section shall apply to transactions duly consummated pursuant to authority given by the Secretary of Transportation, Federal Power Commission, Surface Transportation Board, the Securities and Exchange Commission in the exercise of its jurisdiction under , the United States Maritime Commission, or the summary.one_week_summary: 15 U.S.C. - Liability of directors and agents of corporation: Whenever a corporation shall violate any of the penal provisions of the antitrust laws, such violation shall be deemed to be also that of the individual directors, officers, or agents of such corporation who shall have authorized, ordered, or done any of the acts constituting in whole or in part such violation, and such violation shall be deemed a misdemeanor, and upon conviction therefor of any such director, officer, or agent he shall be punished by a fine of not exceeding $5,000 or by imprisonment for not exceeding one year, or by both, in the discretion of the court.

US-15-USC-25.title: 15 U.S.C. § 25 - Restraining violations; procedure

summary.one_week_summary: 15 U.S.C. - Restraining violations; procedure: The several district courts of the United States are invested with jurisdiction to prevent and restrain violations of this Act, and it shall be the duty of the several United States attorneys, in their respective districts, under the direction of the Attorney General, to institute proceedings in equity to prevent and restrain such violations.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under 15 U.S.C. regarding restraining violations; procedure.

US-15-USC-25.full_text: The several district courts of the United States are invested with jurisdiction to prevent and restrain violations of this Act, and it shall be the duty of the several United States attorneys, in their respective districts, under the direction of the Attorney General, to institute proceedings in equity to prevent and restrain such violations. Such proceedings may be by way of petition setting forth the case and praying that such violation shall be enjoined or otherwise prohibited. When the parties complained of shall have been duly notified of such petition, the court shall proceed, as soon as may be, to the hearing and determination of the case; and pending such petition, and before final decree, the court may at any time make such temporary restraining order or prohibition as shall be deemed just in the premises. Whenever it shall appear to the court before which any such proceeding may be pending that the ends of justice require that other parties should be brought before the court, the court may cause them to be summoned whether they reside in the district in which the court is held or not, and subpoenas to that end may be served in any district by the marshal thereof.

summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under 15 U.S.C. regarding injunctive relief for private parties; exception; costs.

summary.one_week_summary: 15 U.S.C. - Federal Trade Commission established; membership; vacancies; seal: A commission is created and established, to be known as the Federal Trade Commission (hereinafter referred to as the Commission), which shall be composed of five Commissioners, who shall be appointed by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under 15 U.S.C. regarding federal trade commission established; membership; vacancies; seal.

US-15-USC-41.full_text: A commission is created and established, to be known as the Federal Trade Commission (hereinafter referred to as the Commission), which shall be composed of five Commissioners, who shall be appointed by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate. Not more than three of the Commissioners shall be members of the same political party. The first Commissioners appointed shall continue in office for terms of three, four, five, six, and seven years, respectively, from , the term of each to be designated by the President, but their successors shall be appointed for terms of seven years, except that any person chosen to fill a vacancy shall be appointed only for the unexpired term of the Commissioner whom he shall succeed: , That upon the expiration of his term of office a Commissioner shall continue to serve until his successor shall have been appointed and shall have qualified.. The President shall choose a chairman from the Commission’s membership. No Commissioner shall engage in any other business, vocation, or employment. Any Commissioner may be removed by the President for inefficiency, neglect of duty, or malfeasance in office. A vacancy in the Commission shall not impair the right of the remaining Commissioners to exercise all the powers of the Commission.September 26, 1914Provided, however1So in original.1The Commission shall have an official seal, which shall be judicially noticed.

US-15-USC-42.full_text: Each commissioner shall receive a salary, payable in the same manner as the salaries of the judges of the courts of the United States. The commission shall appoint a secretary, who shall receive a salary, and it shall have authority to employ and fix the compensation of such attorneys, special experts, examiners, clerks, and other employees as it may from time to time find necessary for the proper performance of its duties and as may be from time to time appropriated for by Congress.With the exception of the secretary, a clerk to each Commissioner, the attorneys, and such special experts and examiners as the Commission may from time to time find necessary for the conduct of its work, all employees of the Commission shall be a part of the classified civil service, and shall enter the service under such rules and regulations as may be prescribed by the Commission and by the Director of the Office of Personnel Management.All of the expenses of the Commission, including all necessary expenses for transportation incurred by the Commissioners or by their employees under their orders, in making any investigation, or upon official business in any other places than in the city of Washington, shall be allowed and paid on the presentation of itemized vouchers therefor approved by the Commission.Until otherwise provided by law, the Commission may rent suitable offices for its use.The Government Accountability Office shall receive and examine all accounts of expenditures of the Commission.

US-15-USC-49.title: 15 U.S.C. § 49 - Documentary evidence; depositions; witnesses

summary.one_week_summary: 15 U.S.C. - Documentary evidence; depositions; witnesses: For the purposes of this subchapter the Commission, or its duly authorized agent or agents, shall at all reasonable times have access to, for the purpose of examination, and the right to copy any documentary evidence of any person, partnership, or corporation being investigated or proceeded against; and the Commission shall have power to require by subpoena the attendance and testimony of witnesses and the production of all such documentary evidence relating to any matter under investigation.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under 15 U.S.C. regarding documentary evidence; depositions; witnesses.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

US-15-USC-49.full_text: For the purposes of this subchapter the Commission, or its duly authorized agent or agents, shall at all reasonable times have access to, for the purpose of examination, and the right to copy any documentary evidence of any person, partnership, or corporation being investigated or proceeded against; and the Commission shall have power to require by subpoena the attendance and testimony of witnesses and the production of all such documentary evidence relating to any matter under investigation. Any member of the Commission may sign subpoenas, and members and examiners of the Commission may administer oaths and affirmations, examine witnesses, and receive evidence.Such attendance of witnesses, and the production of such documentary evidence, may be required from any place in the United States, at any designated place of hearing. And in case of disobedience to a subpoena the Commission may invoke the aid of any court of the United States in requiring the attendance and testimony of witnesses and the production of documentary evidence.Any of the district courts of the United States within the jurisdiction of which such inquiry is carried on may, in case of contumacy or refusal to obey a subpoena issued to any person, partnership, or corporation issue an order requiring such person, partnership, or corporation to appear before the Commission, or to produce documentary evidence if so ordered, or to give evidence touching the matter in question; and any failure to obey such order of the court may be punished by such court as a contempt thereof.Upon the application of the Attorney General of the United States, at the request of the Commission, the district courts of the United States shall have jurisdiction to issue writs of mandamus commanding any person, partnership, or corporation to comply with the provisions of this subchapter or any order of the Commission made in pursuance thereof.The Commission may order testimony to be taken by deposition in any proceeding or investigation pending under this subchapter at any stage of such proceeding or investigation. Such depositions may be taken before any person designated by the commission and having power to administer oaths. Such testimony shall be reduced to writing by the person taking the deposition, or under his direction, and shall then be subscribed by the deponent. Any person may be compelled to appear and depose and to produce documentary evidence in the same manner as witnesses may be compelled to appear and testify and produce documentary evidence before the Commission as hereinbefore provided.Witnesses summoned before the Commission shall be paid the same fees and mileage that are paid witnesses in the courts of the United States and witnesses whose depositions are taken and the persons taking the same shall severally be entitled to the same fees as are paid for like services in the courts of the United States.

US-15-USC-50.title: 15 U.S.C. § 50 - Offenses and penalties

summary.one_week_summary: 15 U.S.C. - Offenses and penalties: Any person who shall neglect or refuse to attend and testify, or to answer any lawful inquiry or to produce any documentary evidence, if in his power to do so, in obedience to an order of a district court of the United States directing compliance with the subpoena or lawful requirement of the Commission, shall be guilty of an offense and upon conviction thereof by a court of competent jurisdiction shall be punished by a fine of not less than $1,000 nor more than $5,000, or by imprisonment for not more than one year, or by both such fine and imprisonment.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under 15 U.S.C. regarding offenses and penalties.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

US-15-USC-50.full_text: Any person who shall neglect or refuse to attend and testify, or to answer any lawful inquiry or to produce any documentary evidence, if in his power to do so, in obedience to an order of a district court of the United States directing compliance with the subpoena or lawful requirement of the Commission, shall be guilty of an offense and upon conviction thereof by a court of competent jurisdiction shall be punished by a fine of not less than $1,000 nor more than $5,000, or by imprisonment for not more than one year, or by both such fine and imprisonment.Any person who shall willfully make, or cause to be made, any false entry or statement of fact in any report required to be made under this subchapter, or who shall willfully make, or cause to be made, any false entry in any account, record, or memorandum kept by any person, partnership, or corporation subject to this subchapter, or who shall willfully neglect or fail to make, or to cause to be made, full, true, and correct entries in such accounts, records, or memoranda of all facts and transactions appertaining to the business of such person, partnership, or corporation, or who shall willfully remove out of the jurisdiction of the United States, or willfully mutilate, alter, or by any other means falsify any documentary evidence of such person, partnership, or corporation, or who shall willfully refuse to submit to the Commission or to any of its authorized agents, for the purpose of inspection and taking copies, any documentary evidence of such person, partnership, or corporation in his possession or within his control, shall be deemed guilty of an offense against the United States, and shall be subject, upon conviction in any court of the United States of competent jurisdiction, to a fine of not less than $1,000 nor more than $5,000, or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both such fine and imprisonment.If any persons, partnership, or corporation required by this subchapter to file any annual or special report shall fail so to do within the time fixed by the Commission for filing the same, and such failure shall continue for thirty days after notice of such default, the corporation shall forfeit to the United States the sum of $100 for each and every day of the continuance of such failure, which forfeiture shall be payable into the Treasury of the United States, and shall be recoverable in a civil suit in the name of the United States brought in the case of a corporation or partnership in the district where the corporation or partnership has its principal office or in any district in which it shall do business, and in the case of any person in the district where such person resides or has his principal place of business. It shall be the duty of the various United States attorneys, under the direction of the Attorney General of the United States, to prosecute for the recovery of the forfeitures. The costs and expenses of such prosecution shall be paid out of the appropriation for the expenses of the courts of the United States.Any officer or employee of the Commission who shall make public any information obtained by the Commission without its authority, unless directed by a court, shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by a fine not exceeding $5,000, or by imprisonment not exceeding one year, or by fine and imprisonment, in the discretion of the court.

EU-REG-139-2004:Art.2.title: EUMR 139/2004, Art. 2 - merger test

summary.one_week_summary: EUMR 139/2004, Art. 2 (merger test): Concentrations that significantly impede effective competition are incompatible with the internal market.
summary.operative_rule: Concentrations that significantly impede effective competition are incompatible with the internal market.

EU-REG-139-2004:Art.2.full_text: Concentrations that significantly impede effective competition are incompatible with the internal market.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.2.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.2 - definitions and contract formation

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.2 (definitions and contract formation): Defines fundamental terms: proposal, acceptance, promise, consideration, agreement, reciprocal promises, void agreements, and enforceable contracts.
summary.operative_rule: Defines fundamental terms: proposal, acceptance, promise, consideration, agreement, reciprocal promises, void agreements, and enforceable contracts.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.2.full_text: Defines fundamental terms: proposal, acceptance, promise, consideration, agreement, reciprocal promises, void agreements, and enforceable contracts.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.11.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.11 - capacity of parties to contract

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.11 (capacity of parties to contract): Parties must be of the age of majority according to the law to which they are subject, sound mind, and not disqualified from contracting by any law.
summary.operative_rule: Parties must be of the age of majority according to the law to which they are subject, sound mind, and not disqualified from contracting by any law.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.11.full_text: Parties must be of the age of majority according to the law to which they are subject, sound mind, and not disqualified from contracting by any law.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.15.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.15 - coercion

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.15 (coercion): Coercion is committing or threatening to commit any act forbidden by the Penal Code, or unlawful detaining of property to compel consent.
summary.operative_rule: Coercion is committing or threatening to commit any act forbidden by the Penal Code, or unlawful detaining of property to compel consent.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.15.full_text: Coercion is committing or threatening to commit any act forbidden by the Penal Code, or unlawful detaining of property to compel consent.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.17.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.17 - fraud

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.17 (fraud): Fraud includes suggestion as a fact of that which is not true, active concealment, promise made without intention to perform, or deceptive acts to induce contract.
summary.operative_rule: Fraud includes suggestion as a fact of that which is not true, active concealment, promise made without intention to perform, or deceptive acts to induce contract.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.17.full_text: Fraud includes suggestion as a fact of that which is not true, active concealment, promise made without intention to perform, or deceptive acts to induce contract.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.18.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.18 - misrepresentation

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.18 (misrepresentation): Positive assertion not warranted by information, breach of duty causing mistake, or causing a party to make mistake as to substance of contract subject matter.
summary.operative_rule: Positive assertion not warranted by information, breach of duty causing mistake, or causing a party to make mistake as to substance of contract subject matter.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.18.full_text: Positive assertion not warranted by information, breach of duty causing mistake, or causing a party to make mistake as to substance of contract subject matter.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.19.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.19 - voidability of agreements without free consent

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.19 (voidability of agreements without free consent): Agreements caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation are voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.
summary.operative_rule: Agreements caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation are voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.19.full_text: Agreements caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation are voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.20.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.20 - mutual mistake of fact

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.20 (mutual mistake of fact): Agreement void where both parties are under a mistake as to a matter of fact essential to the agreement.
summary.operative_rule: Agreement void where both parties are under a mistake as to a matter of fact essential to the agreement.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.20.full_text: Agreement void where both parties are under a mistake as to a matter of fact essential to the agreement.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.24.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.24 - agreements void if consideration unlawful in part

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.24 (agreements void if consideration unlawful in part): If any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or any one of any part of any one of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful, agreement is void.
summary.operative_rule: If any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or any one of any part of any one of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful, agreement is void.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.24.full_text: If any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or any one of any part of any one of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful, agreement is void.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.25.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.25 - agreements without consideration

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.25 (agreements without consideration): Agreement made without consideration is void unless expressed in writing and registered, or made on account of natural love and affection, or promise to compensate past voluntary services.
summary.operative_rule: Agreement made without consideration is void unless expressed in writing and registered, or made on account of natural love and affection, or promise to compensate past voluntary services.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.25.full_text: Agreement made without consideration is void unless expressed in writing and registered, or made on account of natural love and affection, or promise to compensate past voluntary services.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.29.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.29 - agreements void for uncertainty

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.29 (agreements void for uncertainty): Agreements, the meaning of which is not certain, or capable of being made certain, are void.
summary.operative_rule: Agreements, the meaning of which is not certain, or capable of being made certain, are void.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.29.full_text: Agreements, the meaning of which is not certain, or capable of being made certain, are void.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.37.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.37 - obligation of parties to perform contracts

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.37 (obligation of parties to perform contracts): Parties to a contract must either perform, or offer to perform, their respective promises, unless performance is dispensed with or excused.
summary.operative_rule: Parties to a contract must either perform, or offer to perform, their respective promises, unless performance is dispensed with or excused.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.37.full_text: Parties to a contract must either perform, or offer to perform, their respective promises, unless performance is dispensed with or excused.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.55.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.55 - time as essence of contract

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.55 (time as essence of contract): When a party promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, and fails to do so, contract becomes voidable at option of promisee if intention was that time should be of essence.
summary.operative_rule: When a party promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, and fails to do so, contract becomes voidable at option of promisee if intention was that time should be of essence.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.55.full_text: When a party promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, and fails to do so, contract becomes voidable at option of promisee if intention was that time should be of essence.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.56.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.56 - doctrine of frustration and impossibility

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.56 (doctrine of frustration and impossibility): Agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. A contract to do an act which becomes impossible or unlawful after contracting becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful.
summary.operative_rule: Agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. A contract to do an act which becomes impossible or unlawful after contracting becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.56.full_text: Agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. A contract to do an act which becomes impossible or unlawful after contracting becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.62.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.62 - effect of novation, rescission, and alteration

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.62 (effect of novation, rescission, and alteration): If parties to a contract agree to substitute a new contract for it, or to rescind or alter it, original contract need not be performed.
summary.operative_rule: If parties to a contract agree to substitute a new contract for it, or to rescind or alter it, original contract need not be performed.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.62.full_text: If parties to a contract agree to substitute a new contract for it, or to rescind or alter it, original contract need not be performed.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.63.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.63 - dispensation or remission of performance

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.63 (dispensation or remission of performance): Promisee may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part, performance of promise, or extend time, or accept any satisfaction.
summary.operative_rule: Promisee may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part, performance of promise, or extend time, or accept any satisfaction.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.63.full_text: Promisee may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part, performance of promise, or extend time, or accept any satisfaction.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.65.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.65 - obligation to restore advantage under void agreement

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.65 (obligation to restore advantage under void agreement): When an agreement is discovered to be void, or contract becomes void, person who received advantage is bound to restore it or compensate.
summary.operative_rule: When an agreement is discovered to be void, or contract becomes void, person who received advantage is bound to restore it or compensate.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.65.full_text: When an agreement is discovered to be void, or contract becomes void, person who received advantage is bound to restore it or compensate.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.125.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.125 - rights of indemnity-holder

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.125 (rights of indemnity-holder): Indemnity-holder acting within authority can recover damages, costs of defense, and sums paid under compromise.
summary.operative_rule: Indemnity-holder acting within authority can recover damages, costs of defense, and sums paid under compromise.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.125.full_text: Indemnity-holder acting within authority can recover damages, costs of defense, and sums paid under compromise.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.126.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.126 - contract of guarantee and surety

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.126 (contract of guarantee and surety): Defines contract of guarantee to perform promise, or discharge liability, of a third person in case of default. Parties: surety, principal debtor, creditor.
summary.operative_rule: Defines contract of guarantee to perform promise, or discharge liability, of a third person in case of default. Parties: surety, principal debtor, creditor.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.126.full_text: Defines contract of guarantee to perform promise, or discharge liability, of a third person in case of default. Parties: surety, principal debtor, creditor.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.128.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.128 - surety's liability co-extensive

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.128 (surety's liability co-extensive): Liability of the surety is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor, unless otherwise provided by the contract.
summary.operative_rule: Liability of the surety is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor, unless otherwise provided by the contract.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.128.full_text: Liability of the surety is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor, unless otherwise provided by the contract.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.133.title: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.133 - discharge of surety by variance in terms

summary.one_week_summary: Contract Act 1872 (BD), s.133 (discharge of surety by variance in terms): Any variance made without surety's consent in terms of contract between principal debtor and creditor discharges surety as to transactions subsequent to variance.
summary.operative_rule: Any variance made without surety's consent in terms of contract between principal debtor and creditor discharges surety as to transactions subsequent to variance.

BD-CONTRACT-1872:s.133.full_text: Any variance made without surety's consent in terms of contract between principal debtor and creditor discharges surety as to transactions subsequent to variance.

BD-COMP-2012:s.2.title: Competition Act 2012 (BD), s.2 - definitions of competition law terms

summary.one_week_summary: Competition Act 2012 (BD), s.2 (definitions of competition law terms): Defines agreement, enterprise, cartel, turnover, dominant position, goods, market, predatory price, and vertical arrangements.
summary.operative_rule: Defines agreement, enterprise, cartel, turnover, dominant position, goods, market, predatory price, and vertical arrangements.

BD-COMP-2012:s.2.full_text: Defines agreement, enterprise, cartel, turnover, dominant position, goods, market, predatory price, and vertical arrangements.

BD-COMP-2012:s.3.title: Competition Act 2012 (BD), s.3 - extraterritorial application

summary.one_week_summary: Competition Act 2012 (BD), s.3 (extraterritorial application): The Commission has power to inquire into agreements, dominant abuse or combinations taking place outside Bangladesh if they have an appreciable adverse effect on competition within Bangladesh.
summary.operative_rule: The Commission has power to inquire into agreements, dominant abuse or combinations taking place outside Bangladesh if they have an appreciable adverse effect on competition within Bangladesh.

BD-COMP-2012:s.3.full_text: The Commission has power to inquire into agreements, dominant abuse or combinations taking place outside Bangladesh if they have an appreciable adverse effect on competition within Bangladesh.

BD-COMP-2012:s.8.title: Competition Act 2012 (BD), s.8 - powers and functions of Competition Commission

summary.one_week_summary: Competition Act 2012 (BD), s.8 (powers and functions of Competition Commission): Commission is empowered to eliminate anti-competitive practices, promote and sustain competition, protect consumer interests, and ensure freedom of trade.
summary.operative_rule: Commission is empowered to eliminate anti-competitive practices, promote and sustain competition, protect consumer interests, and ensure freedom of trade.

BD-COMP-2012:s.8.full_text: Commission is empowered to eliminate anti-competitive practices, promote and sustain competition, protect consumer interests, and ensure freedom of trade.

BD-COMP-2012:s.16(2).title: Competition Act 2012 (BD), s.16(2) - prohibited practices of dominant abuse

summary.one_week_summary: Competition Act 2012 (BD), s.16(2) (prohibited practices of dominant abuse): Presumed abuses include unfair/discriminatory pricing, predatory pricing below production cost, limiting technical development, denying market access, or making contract conclusion subject to supplementary obligations.
summary.operative_rule: Presumed abuses include unfair/discriminatory pricing, predatory pricing below production cost, limiting technical development, denying market access, or making contract conclusion subject to supplementary obligations.

BD-COMP-2012:s.16(2).full_text: Presumed abuses include unfair/discriminatory pricing, predatory pricing below production cost, limiting technical development, denying market access, or making contract conclusion subject to supplementary obligations.

BD-COMP-2012:s.36.title: Competition Act 2012 (BD), s.36 - appeals to High Court Division

summary.one_week_summary: Competition Act 2012 (BD), s.36 (appeals to High Court Division): Any person aggrieved by an order or decision of the Bangladesh Competition Commission may appeal to the High Court Division within 60 days.
summary.operative_rule: Any person aggrieved by an order or decision of the Bangladesh Competition Commission may appeal to the High Court Division within 60 days.

BD-COMP-2012:s.36.full_text: Any person aggrieved by an order or decision of the Bangladesh Competition Commission may appeal to the High Court Division within 60 days.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.4.title: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.4 - sale and agreement to sell

summary.one_week_summary: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.4 (sale and agreement to sell): Contract of sale of goods is a contract whereby seller transfers or agrees to transfer property in goods to buyer for price. Agreement to sell becomes sale when time elapses or conditions fulfilled.
summary.operative_rule: Contract of sale of goods is a contract whereby seller transfers or agrees to transfer property in goods to buyer for price. Agreement to sell becomes sale when time elapses or conditions fulfilled.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.4.full_text: Contract of sale of goods is a contract whereby seller transfers or agrees to transfer property in goods to buyer for price. Agreement to sell becomes sale when time elapses or conditions fulfilled.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.12.title: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.12 - condition and warranty distinguished

summary.one_week_summary: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.12 (condition and warranty distinguished): Condition is a stipulation essential to main purpose of contract, breach of which gives right to treat contract as repudiated. Warranty is collateral, giving right to claim damages only.
summary.operative_rule: Condition is a stipulation essential to main purpose of contract, breach of which gives right to treat contract as repudiated. Warranty is collateral, giving right to claim damages only.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.12.full_text: Condition is a stipulation essential to main purpose of contract, breach of which gives right to treat contract as repudiated. Warranty is collateral, giving right to claim damages only.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.14.title: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.14 - implied condition as to title and quiet possession

summary.one_week_summary: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.14 (implied condition as to title and quiet possession): Implied condition that seller has right to sell goods, and implied warranty that buyer shall have and enjoy quiet possession free from undisclosed third-party encumbrances.
summary.operative_rule: Implied condition that seller has right to sell goods, and implied warranty that buyer shall have and enjoy quiet possession free from undisclosed third-party encumbrances.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.14.full_text: Implied condition that seller has right to sell goods, and implied warranty that buyer shall have and enjoy quiet possession free from undisclosed third-party encumbrances.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.16.title: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.16 - implied condition of merchantable quality and fitness

summary.one_week_summary: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.16 (implied condition of merchantable quality and fitness): Implied condition that goods shall be reasonably fit for purpose disclosed to seller where buyer relies on seller's skill, and of merchantable quality where goods bought by description.
summary.operative_rule: Implied condition that goods shall be reasonably fit for purpose disclosed to seller where buyer relies on seller's skill, and of merchantable quality where goods bought by description.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.16.full_text: Implied condition that goods shall be reasonably fit for purpose disclosed to seller where buyer relies on seller's skill, and of merchantable quality where goods bought by description.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.27.title: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.27 - sale by person not the owner

summary.one_week_summary: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.27 (sale by person not the owner): Nemo dat quod non habet principle: buyer acquires no better title than seller had, unless owner is precluded by conduct or sale is by mercantile agent in ordinary course of business.
summary.operative_rule: Nemo dat quod non habet principle: buyer acquires no better title than seller had, unless owner is precluded by conduct or sale is by mercantile agent in ordinary course of business.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.27.full_text: Nemo dat quod non habet principle: buyer acquires no better title than seller had, unless owner is precluded by conduct or sale is by mercantile agent in ordinary course of business.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.55.title: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.55 - suit for price

summary.one_week_summary: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.55 (suit for price): Where property in goods has passed to buyer and buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to pay, seller may sue for price of goods.
summary.operative_rule: Where property in goods has passed to buyer and buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to pay, seller may sue for price of goods.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.55.full_text: Where property in goods has passed to buyer and buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to pay, seller may sue for price of goods.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.56.title: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.56 - damages for non-acceptance

summary.one_week_summary: Sale of Goods Act 1930 (BD), s.56 (damages for non-acceptance): Where buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to accept and pay for goods, seller may sue for damages for non-acceptance measured by natural and direct loss.
summary.operative_rule: Where buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to accept and pay for goods, seller may sue for damages for non-acceptance measured by natural and direct loss.

BD-SOGA-1930:s.56.full_text: Where buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to accept and pay for goods, seller may sue for damages for non-acceptance measured by natural and direct loss.

BD-ARB-2001:s.7.title: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.7 - judicial non-intervention in arbitration

summary.one_week_summary: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.7 (judicial non-intervention in arbitration): Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, no judicial authority shall intervene in matters governed by the Act except as specifically provided.
summary.operative_rule: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, no judicial authority shall intervene in matters governed by the Act except as specifically provided.

BD-ARB-2001:s.7.full_text: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, no judicial authority shall intervene in matters governed by the Act except as specifically provided.

BD-ARB-2001:s.9.title: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.9 - form of arbitration agreement

summary.one_week_summary: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.9 (form of arbitration agreement): Arbitration agreement must be in writing (document signed by parties, exchange of letters, telex, telegrams, emails, or claim/defense admissions).
summary.operative_rule: Arbitration agreement must be in writing (document signed by parties, exchange of letters, telex, telegrams, emails, or claim/defense admissions).

BD-ARB-2001:s.9.full_text: Arbitration agreement must be in writing (document signed by parties, exchange of letters, telex, telegrams, emails, or claim/defense admissions).

BD-ARB-2001:s.10.title: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.10 - stay of legal proceedings for arbitration

summary.one_week_summary: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.10 (stay of legal proceedings for arbitration): Court must refer parties to arbitration upon application by a party to an arbitration agreement before filing written statement on the substance of the dispute.
summary.operative_rule: Court must refer parties to arbitration upon application by a party to an arbitration agreement before filing written statement on the substance of the dispute.

BD-ARB-2001:s.10.full_text: Court must refer parties to arbitration upon application by a party to an arbitration agreement before filing written statement on the substance of the dispute.

BD-ARB-2001:s.11.title: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.11 - interim measures by court

summary.one_week_summary: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.11 (interim measures by court): Court has power before or during arbitral proceedings to grant interim preservation, custody, or sale of goods, detention, or interim injunctions.
summary.operative_rule: Court has power before or during arbitral proceedings to grant interim preservation, custody, or sale of goods, detention, or interim injunctions.

BD-ARB-2001:s.11.full_text: Court has power before or during arbitral proceedings to grant interim preservation, custody, or sale of goods, detention, or interim injunctions.

BD-ARB-2001:s.17.title: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.17 - kompetenz-kompetenz jurisdiction of tribunal

summary.one_week_summary: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.17 (kompetenz-kompetenz jurisdiction of tribunal): Arbitral tribunal may rule on its own jurisdiction, including ruling on any objections with respect to the existence or validity of the arbitration agreement.
summary.operative_rule: Arbitral tribunal may rule on its own jurisdiction, including ruling on any objections with respect to the existence or validity of the arbitration agreement.

BD-ARB-2001:s.17.full_text: Arbitral tribunal may rule on its own jurisdiction, including ruling on any objections with respect to the existence or validity of the arbitration agreement.

BD-ARB-2001:s.42.title: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.42 - grounds for setting aside arbitral award

summary.one_week_summary: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.42 (grounds for setting aside arbitral award): High Court or District Court may set aside award only if party under incapacity, agreement invalid, lack of proper notice, dispute outside scope, or award in conflict with public policy of Bangladesh.
summary.operative_rule: High Court or District Court may set aside award only if party under incapacity, agreement invalid, lack of proper notice, dispute outside scope, or award in conflict with public policy of Bangladesh.

BD-ARB-2001:s.42.full_text: High Court or District Court may set aside award only if party under incapacity, agreement invalid, lack of proper notice, dispute outside scope, or award in conflict with public policy of Bangladesh.

BD-ARB-2001:s.45.title: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.45 - enforcement of domestic arbitral awards

summary.one_week_summary: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.45 (enforcement of domestic arbitral awards): Where time for setting aside expired or application rejected, arbitral award shall be enforced under Code of Civil Procedure in the same manner as a decree of court.
summary.operative_rule: Where time for setting aside expired or application rejected, arbitral award shall be enforced under Code of Civil Procedure in the same manner as a decree of court.

BD-ARB-2001:s.45.full_text: Where time for setting aside expired or application rejected, arbitral award shall be enforced under Code of Civil Procedure in the same manner as a decree of court.

BD-ARB-2001:s.46.title: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.46 - recognition and enforcement of foreign arbitral awards

summary.one_week_summary: Arbitration Act 2001 (BD), s.46 (recognition and enforcement of foreign arbitral awards): Foreign arbitral award made in a reciprocating New York Convention state shall be recognized as binding and enforceable in Bangladesh.
summary.operative_rule: Foreign arbitral award made in a reciprocating New York Convention state shall be recognized as binding and enforceable in Bangladesh.

BD-ARB-2001:s.46.full_text: Foreign arbitral award made in a reciprocating New York Convention state shall be recognized as binding and enforceable in Bangladesh.

BD-SRA-1877:s.12.title: Specific Relief Act 1877 (BD), s.12 - specific performance of contracts

summary.one_week_summary: Specific Relief Act 1877 (BD), s.12 (specific performance of contracts): Specific performance enforceable when agreed act is unquantifiable in pecuniary damages, or when pecuniary compensation cannot afford adequate relief.
summary.operative_rule: Specific performance enforceable when agreed act is unquantifiable in pecuniary damages, or when pecuniary compensation cannot afford adequate relief.

BD-SRA-1877:s.12.full_text: Specific performance enforceable when agreed act is unquantifiable in pecuniary damages, or when pecuniary compensation cannot afford adequate relief.

BD-SRA-1877:s.21.title: Specific Relief Act 1877 (BD), s.21 - contracts not specifically enforceable

summary.one_week_summary: Specific Relief Act 1877 (BD), s.21 (contracts not specifically enforceable): Contracts for the non-performance of which compensation in money is adequate relief, contracts running into minute details, contracts of personal service, and contracts revocable in nature cannot be specifically enforced.
summary.operative_rule: Contracts for the non-performance of which compensation in money is adequate relief, contracts running into minute details, contracts of personal service, and contracts revocable in nature cannot be specifically enforced.

BD-SRA-1877:s.21.full_text: Contracts for the non-performance of which compensation in money is adequate relief, contracts running into minute details, contracts of personal service, and contracts revocable in nature cannot be specifically enforced.

BD-SRA-1877:s.54.title: Specific Relief Act 1877 (BD), s.54 - perpetual injunctions

summary.one_week_summary: Specific Relief Act 1877 (BD), s.54 (perpetual injunctions): Perpetual injunction granted to prevent breach of obligation where defendant invades plaintiff's rights and pecuniary compensation cannot afford adequate relief.
summary.operative_rule: Perpetual injunction granted to prevent breach of obligation where defendant invades plaintiff's rights and pecuniary compensation cannot afford adequate relief.

BD-SRA-1877:s.54.full_text: Perpetual injunction granted to prevent breach of obligation where defendant invades plaintiff's rights and pecuniary compensation cannot afford adequate relief.

BD-SRA-1877:s.57.title: Specific Relief Act 1877 (BD), s.57 - injunction to perform negative agreement

summary.one_week_summary: Specific Relief Act 1877 (BD), s.57 (injunction to perform negative agreement): Where a contract comprises an affirmative agreement to do a certain act, coupled with a negative agreement not to do a certain act, court may grant injunction to perform negative agreement even if affirmative agreement cannot be specifically enforced.
summary.operative_rule: Where a contract comprises an affirmative agreement to do a certain act, coupled with a negative agreement not to do a certain act, court may grant injunction to perform negative agreement even if affirmative agreement cannot be specifically enforced.

BD-SRA-1877:s.57.full_text: Where a contract comprises an affirmative agreement to do a certain act, coupled with a negative agreement not to do a certain act, court may grant injunction to perform negative agreement even if affirmative agreement cannot be specifically enforced.

BD-COMPANIES-1994:s.23.title: Companies Act 1994 (BD), s.23 - binding effect of memorandum and articles

summary.one_week_summary: Companies Act 1994 (BD), s.23 (binding effect of memorandum and articles): Memorandum and articles bind company and members as if signed and sealed by each member to observe all provisions.
summary.operative_rule: Memorandum and articles bind company and members as if signed and sealed by each member to observe all provisions.

BD-COMPANIES-1994:s.23.full_text: Memorandum and articles bind company and members as if signed and sealed by each member to observe all provisions.

BD-COMPANIES-1994:s.103.title: Companies Act 1994 (BD), s.103 - form and validity of company contracts

summary.one_week_summary: Companies Act 1994 (BD), s.103 (form and validity of company contracts): Contracts on behalf of a company may be made in writing under common seal, or in writing signed by any person acting under express or implied authority.

BD-LABOUR-2006:s.27.full_text: Permanent worker may resign by giving 30 days notice to employer. Workers with 5+ years of continuous service are entitled to gratuity or separation compensation.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.1.title: Title and extent of operation of the Code

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Title and extent of operation of the Code: 1.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding title and extent of operation of the code.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.1.full_text: 1. This Act shall be called the Penal Code, and shall take effect throughout Bangladesh.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.2.title: Punishment of offences committed within Bangladesh

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment of offences committed within Bangladesh: 2.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment of offences committed within bangladesh.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.2.full_text: 2. Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Code and not otherwise for every act or omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within Bangladesh.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.3.title: Punishment of offences committed beyond, but which by law may be tried within Bangladesh

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment of offences committed beyond, but which by law may be tried within Bangladesh: 3.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment of offences committed beyond, but which by law may be tried within bangladesh.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.3.full_text: 3. Any person liable, by any Bangladesh Law, to be tried for an offence committed beyond Bangladesh shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Code for any act committed beyond Bangladesh in the same manner as if such act had been committed within Bangladesh

BD-PENAL-1860:s.4.title: Extension of Code to extra-territorial offences

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Extension of Code to extra-territorial offences: 4.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding extension of code to extra-territorial offences.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.4.full_text:
4. The provisions of this Code apply also to any offence committed by-
(1) any citizen of Bangladesh in any place without and beyond Bangladesh;
(2) [Omitted by Article 2 and Schedule of the Central Laws (Adaptation) Order, 1961.]
(3) [Omitted by section 3 and 2nd Schedule of the Bangladesh Laws (Revision And Declaration) Act, 1973 (Act No. VIII of 1973).]
(4) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in Bangladesh wherever it may be.
Explanation.-In this section the word "offence" includes every act committed outside Bangladesh which, if committed in Bangladesh, would be punishable under this Code.
Illustrations
(a) A, a Bangladesh subject, commits a murder in Uganda. He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in Bangladesh in which he may be found.
(b) B, a European British subject, commits a murder in Rangpur. He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in Bangladesh in which he may be found.
(c) C, a foreigner who is in the service of the Bangladesh Government, commits a murder in Khulna. He can be tried and convicted of murder at any place in Bangladesh in which he may be found.
(d) D, a British subject living in Khulna, instigates E to commit a murder in Chittagong. D is guilty of abetting murder.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.5.title: Certain laws not to be affected by this Act

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Certain laws not to be affected by this Act: 5.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding certain laws not to be affected by this act.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.5.full_text: 5. Nothing in this Act is intended to repeal, vary, suspend, or affect any of the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Republic, or of any special or local law.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.6.title: Definitions in the Code to be understood subject to exceptions

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Definitions in the Code to be understood subject to exceptions: 6.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding definitions in the code to be understood subject to exceptions.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.6.full_text:
6. Throughout this Code every definition of an offence, every penal provision and every illustration of every such definition or penal provision, shall be understood subject to the exceptions contained in the chapter entitled "General Exceptions," though those exceptions are not repeated in such definition, penal provision or illustration.
Illustrations
(a) The sections in this Code, which contain definitions of offences, do not express that a child under seven years of age cannot commit such offences; but the definitions are to be understood subject to the general exception which provides that nothing shall be an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age.
(b) A, a police officer, without warrant, apprehends Z who has committed murder. Here A is not guilty of the offence of wrongful confinement; for he was bound by law to apprehend Z, and therefore the case falls within the general exception which provides that "nothing is an offence which is done by a person who is bound by law to do it".

BD-PENAL-1860:s.7.title: Sense of expression once explained

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Sense of expression once explained: 7.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding sense of expression once explained.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.7.full_text: 7. Every expression which is explained in any part of this Code is used in every part of this Code in conformity with the explanation.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.8.title: Gender

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Gender: 8.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding gender.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.8.full_text: 8. The pronoun "he" and its derivatives are used of any person, whether male or female.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.9.title: Number

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Number: 9.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding number.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.9.full_text: 9. Unless the contrary appears from the context, words importing the singular number include the plural number, and words importing the plural number include the singular number.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.10.title: “Man” “Woman”

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - “Man” “Woman”: 10.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding “man” “woman”.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.10.full_text: 10. The word “man” denotes a male human being of any age: the word “woman” denotes a female human being of any age.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.11.title: “Person”

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - “Person”: 11.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding “person”.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.11.full_text: 11. The word “person” includes any Company or Association, or body of persons, whether incorporated or not.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.12.title: “Public”

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - “Public”: 12.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding “public”.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.12.full_text: 12. The word “public” includes any class of the public or any community.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.14.title: “Servant of the State”

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - “Servant of the State”: 14.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding “servant of the state”.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.14.full_text: 14. The words Servant of the Republic denote all officers or servant, continued, appointed or employed in Bangladesh by or under the authority of the Government.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.17.title: “Government”

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - “Government”: 17.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding “government”.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.17.full_text: 17. The word “Government” denotes the person or persons authorized by law to administer executive Government in Bangladesh, or in any part thereof.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.19.title: “Judge”

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - “Judge”: 19.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding “judge”.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.19.full_text:
19. The word “Judge” denotes not only every person who is officially designed as a Judge, but also every person,-
who is empowered by law to give, in any legal proceeding, civil or criminal, a definitive judgment, or a judgment which, if not appealed against, would be definitive, or a judgment which, if confirmed by some other authority, would be definitive, or
who is one of a body of persons, which body of persons is empowered by law to give such a judgment.
Illustrations
(a) A Collector exercising jurisdiction in a suit under Act X of 1859, is a Judge.
(b) A Magistrate exercising jurisdiction in respect of a charge on which he has power to sentence to fine or imprisonment with or without appeal, is a Judge.
(c) [Repealed by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Act 1951 (Act XXXVI of 1951)].
(d) A Magistrate exercising jurisdiction in respect of a charge on which he has power only to commit for trial to another Court, is not a Judge.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.20.title: “Court of justice”

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - “Court of justice”: 20.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding “court of justice”.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.20.full_text: 20. The words "Court of Justice" denote a Judge who is empowered by law to act judicially alone, or a body of Judges which is empowered by law to act judicially as a body, when such Judge or body of Judges is acting judicially.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.21.title: “Public servant”

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - “Public servant”: 21.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding “public servant”.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.22.title: “Moveable property”

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - “Moveable property”: 22.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding “moveable property”.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.22.full_text: 22. The words "moveable property" are intended to include corporeal property of every description, except land and thing attached to the earth or permanently fastened to any thing which is attached to the earth.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.23.title: “Wrongful gain”

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - “Wrongful gain”: 23.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding “wrongful gain”.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.23.full_text: 23. "Wrongful gain" is gain by unlawful means of property to which the person gaining is not legally entitled.

BD-PENAL-1860:s..title: Imputation made in good faith by person for protection of his or other’s interests
