Here if the child was acting under the influence of A's instigation, and the act done was under the circumstances a probable consequence of the abetment, A is liable in the same manner and to the same extent as if he had instigated the child to put the poison into the food of Y.


(b) A instigates B to burn Z's house. B sets fire to the house and at the same time commits theft of property there. A, though guilty of abetting the burning of the house, is not guilty of abetting the theft; for the theft was a distinct act, and not a probable consequence of the burning.

 
 

(c) A instigates B and C to break into an inhabited house at midnight for the purpose of robbery, and provides them with arms for that purpose. B and C break into the house, and being resisted by Z, one of the inmates, murder Z. Here, if that murder was the probable consequence of the abetment, A is liable to the punishment provided for murder.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.112.title: Abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done: 112.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.112.full_text:
112. If the act for which the abettor is liable under the last preceding section is committed in addition to the act abetted, and constitutes a distinct offence, the abettor is liable to punishment for each of the offences.
Illustration
A instigates B to resist by force a distress made by a public servant. B, in consequence, resists that distress. In offering the resistance, B voluntarily causes grievous hurt to the officer executing the distress. As B has committed both the offence of resisting the distress, and the offence of voluntarily causing grievous hurt, B is liable to punishment for both these offences; and, if A knew that B was likely voluntarily to cause grievous hurt in resisting the distress, A will also be liable to punishment for each of the offences.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.113.title: Liability of abettor for an effect caused by the act abetted different from that intended by the abettor

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Liability of abettor for an effect caused by the act abetted different from that intended by the abettor: 113.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding liability of abettor for an effect caused by the act abetted different from that intended by the abettor.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.113.full_text:
113. When an act is abetted with the intention on the part of the abettor of causing a particular effect, and an act for which the abettor is liable in consequence of the abetment, causes a different effect from that intended by the abettor, the abettor is liable for the effect caused, in the same manner and to the same extent as if he had abetted the act with the intention of causing that effect, provided he knew that the act abetted was likely to cause that effect.
Illustration
A instigates B to cause grievous hurt to Z. B, in consequence of the instigation, causes grievous hurt to Z. Z dies in consequence. Here, if A knew that the grievous hurt abetted was likely to cause death, A is liable to be punished with the punishment provided for murder.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.114.title: Abettor present when offence is committed

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abettor present when offence is committed: 114.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abettor present when offence is committed.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.114.full_text: 114. Whenever any person, who if absent would be liable to be punished as an abettor, is present when the act or offence for which he would be punishable in consequence of the abetment is committed, he shall be deemed to have committed such act or offence.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.115.title: Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life- if offence be not committed; if act causing harm be done in consequence

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life- if offence be not committed; if act causing harm be done in consequence: 115.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life- if offence be not committed; if act causing harm be done in consequence.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.115.full_text:
115. Whoever abets the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, shall, if that offence be not committed in consequence of the abetment, and no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such abetment, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine;
and if any act for which the abettor is liable in consequence of the abetment, and which causes hurt to any person, is done, the abettor shall be liable to imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to fourteen years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Illustration
A instigates B to murder Z. The offence is not committed. If B had murdered Z, he would have been subject to the punishment of death or imprisonment for life. Therefore A is liable to imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and also to a fine; and, if any hurt be done to Z in consequence of the abetment, he will be liable to imprisonment for a term which may extend to fourteen years, and to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.116.title: Abetment of offence punishable with imprisonment- if offence be not committed; if abettor or person abetted be a public servant whose duty it is to prevent offence

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abetment of offence punishable with imprisonment- if offence be not committed; if abettor or person abetted be a public servant whose duty it is to prevent offence: 116.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abetment of offence punishable with imprisonment- if offence be not committed; if abettor or person abetted be a public servant whose duty it is to prevent offence.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.116.full_text:
116. Whoever abets an offence punishable with imprisonment shall, if that offence be not committed in consequence of the abetment, and no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such abetment, be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for that offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term provided for that offence; or with such fine as is provided for that offence, or with both;
and if the abettor or the person abetted is a public servant, whose duty it is to prevent the commission of such offence, the abettor shall be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for that offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the longest term provided for that offence, or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or with both.
Illustrations
(a) A offers a bribe to B, a public servant, as a reward for showing A some favour in the exercise of B's official functions. B refuses to accept the bribe. A is punishable under this section.
(b) A instigates B to give false evidence. Here, if B does not give false evidence, A has nevertheless committed the offence defined in this section, and is punishable accordingly.
(c) A, a police-officer, whose duty it is to prevent robbery, abets the commission of robbery. Here, though the robbery be not committed, A is liable to one-half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for that offence, and also to fine.
(d) B abets the commission of a robbery by A, a police-officer, whose duty it is to prevent that offence. Here though the robbery be not committed, B is liable to one-half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offence of robbery, and also to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.117.title: Abetting commission of offence by the public, or by more than ten persons

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abetting commission of offence by the public, or by more than ten persons: 117.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abetting commission of offence by the public, or by more than ten persons.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.117.full_text:
117. Whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
Illustration
A affixes in a public place a placard instigating a sect consisting of more than ten members to meet at a certain time and place, for the purpose of attacking the members of an adverse sect, while engaged in a procession. A has committed the offence defined in this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.118.title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life- if offence be committed; if offence be not committed

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life- if offence be committed; if offence be not committed: 118.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life- if offence be committed; if offence be not committed.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.118.full_text:
118. Whoever intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life,
voluntarily conceals, by any act or illegal omission, the existence of a design to commit such offence or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design,
shall, if that offence be committed, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or, if the offence be not committed, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years; and in either case shall also be liable to fine.
Illustration
A, knowing that dacoity is about to be committed at B, falsely informs the Magistrate that a dacoity is about to be committed at C, a place in an opposite direction, and thereby misleads the Magistrate with intent to facilitate the commission of the offence. The dacoity is committed at B in pursuance of the design. A is punishable under this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.119.title: Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent-

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent-: 119.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent-.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.119.full_text:
119. Whoever, being a public servant intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence which it is his duty as such public servant to prevent,
voluntarily conceals, by any act or illegal omission, the existence of a design to commit such offence, or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design,
shall, if the offence be committed, be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the longest term of such imprisonment, or with such fine as is provided for that offence, or with both;
or, if the offence be punishable with death or imprisonment for life, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years;
or, if the offence be not committed, shall be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of such imprisonment or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or with both.
Illustration
A, an officer of police, being legally bound to give information of all designs to commit robbery which may come to his knowledge, and knowing that B designs to commit robbery, omits to give such information, with intent to facilitate the commission of that offence. Here A has by an illegal omission concealed the existence of B's design, and is liable to punishment according to the provision of this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.120.title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment: 120.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.120.full_text:
120. Whoever, intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable with imprisonment,
voluntarily conceals, by any act or illegal omission, the existence of a design to commit such offence, or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design,
shall, if the offence be committed, be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-fourth, and, if the offence be not committed, to one-eighth, of the longest term of such imprisonment, or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.120A.title: Definition of criminal conspiracy.

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Definition of criminal conspiracy.: 120A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding definition of criminal conspiracy..
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.120A.full_text:
120A. When two or more persons agree to do, or cause to be done,-
(1) an illegal act, or
(2) an act which is not illegal by illegal means, such an agreement is designated a criminal conspiracy:
Provided that no agreement except an agreement to commit an offence shall amount to a criminal conspiracy unless some act besides the agreement is done by one or more parties to such agreement in pursuance thereof.
Explanation.-It is immaterial whether the illegal act is the ultimate object of such agreement, or is merely incidental to that object.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.120B.title: Punishment of criminal conspiracy

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment of criminal conspiracy: 120B.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment of criminal conspiracy.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.120B.full_text:
120B. (1) Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment for a term of two years or upwards, shall, where no express provision is made in this Code for the punishment of such a conspiracy, be punished in the same manner as if he had abetted such offence.
(2) Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy other than a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable as aforesaid shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding six months, or with fine or with both.]

BD-PENAL-1860:s.121.title: Waging or attempting to wage war, or abeting waging of war, against Bangladesh

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Waging or attempting to wage war, or abeting waging of war, against Bangladesh: 121.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding waging or attempting to wage war, or abeting waging of war, against bangladesh.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.121.full_text:
121. Whoever wages war against Bangladesh, or attempts to wage such war, or abets the waging of such war, shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.Illustration
A joins an insurrection against Bangladesh. A has committed the offence defined in this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.121A.title: Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 121.

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 121.: 121A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 121..
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.121A.full_text:
121A. Whoever within or without Bangladesh conspires to commit any of the offences punishable by section 121, or to deprive Bangladesh of the sovereignty of her territories or of any part thereof, or conspires to overawe, by means of criminal force or the show of criminal force, the Government, shall be punished with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment of either description which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.-To constitute a conspiracy under this section, it is not necessary that any act or illegal omission shall take place in pursuance.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.122.title: Collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war against Bangladesh

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war against Bangladesh: 122.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war against bangladesh.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.122.full_text: 122. Whoever collects men, arms or ammunition or otherwise prepares to wage war with the intention of either waging or being prepared to wage war against Bangladesh, shall be punished with imprisonment for life or imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.123.title: Concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war: 123.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.123.full_text: 123. Whoever, by any act, or by any illegal omission, conceals the existence of a design to wage war against Bangladesh, intending by such concealment to facilitate, or knowing it to be likely that such concealment will facilitate the waging of such war, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.123A.title: Condemnation of the creation of the State, and advocacy of abolition of its sovereignty

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Condemnation of the creation of the State, and advocacy of abolition of its sovereignty: 123A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding condemnation of the creation of the state, and advocacy of abolition of its sovereignty.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.123A.full_text:
123A. (I) Whoever, with or without Bangladesh, with intent to influence, or knowing it to be likely that he will influence, any person or the whole or any section of the public, in a manner likely to be prejudicial to the safety of Bangladesh, or to endanger the sovereignty of Bangladesh in respect of all or any of the territories lying within its borders, shall by words, spoken or written, or by signs or visible representation, condemn the creation of Bangladesh in pursuance of the Proclamation of Independence on the twenty-sixth day of March, 1971, or advocate the curtailment or abolition of the sovereignty of Bangladesh in respect of all or any of the territories lying within its borders, whether by amalgamation with the territories of neighboring States or otherwise, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine.
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, when any person is proceeded against under this section, it shall be lawful for any Court before which he may be produced in the course of the investigation or trial, to make such order as it may think fit in respect of his movements, of his association or communication with other persons, and of his activities in regard to dissemination of news, propagation of opinions, until such time as the case is finally decided.
(3) Any Court which is a Court of appeal or of revision in relation to the Court mentioned in sub-section (2) may also make an order under that sub-section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.124.title: Assaulting President, The Government, etc., with intent to compel or restrain the exercise of any lawful power

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Assaulting President, The Government, etc., with intent to compel or restrain the exercise of any lawful power: 124.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding assaulting president, the government, etc., with intent to compel or restrain the exercise of any lawful power.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.124.full_text:
124. Whoever, with the intention of inducing or compelling the President of Bangladesh, or the Government, to exercise or refrain from exercising in any manner any of the lawful powers of the President, or the Government,
assaults, or wrongfully restrains, or attempts wrongfully to restrain, or overawes, by means of criminal force or the show of criminal force, or attempts so to overawe, the President,
shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.124A.title: Sedition

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Sedition: 124A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding sedition.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.124A.full_text:
124A. Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or otherwise, brings or attempts to bring into hatred or contempt, or excites or attempts to excite disaffection towards, the Government established by law shall be punished with imprisonment for life or any shorter term, to which fine may be added, or with imprisonment which may extend to three years, to which fine may be added, or with fine.
Explanation 1.-The expression "disaffection" includes disloyalty and all feelings of enmity.
Explanation 2.-Comments expressing disapprobation of the measures of the Government with a view to obtain their alteration by lawful means, without exciting or attempting to excite hatred, contempt or disaffection, do not constitute an offence under this section.
Explanation 3.-Comments expressing disapprobation of the administrative or other action of the Government without exciting or attempting to excite hatred, contempt or disaffection, do not constitute an offence under this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.125.title: Waging war against any Asiatic Power in alliance with Bangladesh

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Waging war against any Asiatic Power in alliance with Bangladesh: 125.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding waging war against any asiatic power in alliance with bangladesh.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.125.full_text: 125. Whoever wages war against the Government of any Asiatic power in alliance or at peace with Bangladesh or attempts to wage such war, or abets the waging of such war, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, to which fine may be added, or with fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.126.title: Committing depredation on territories of Power at peace with Bangladesh

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Committing depredation on territories of Power at peace with Bangladesh: 126.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding committing depredation on territories of power at peace with bangladesh.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.126.full_text: 126. Whoever commits depredation, or makes preparations to commit depredation, on the territories of any Power in alliance or at peace with Bangladesh, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine and to forfeiture of any property used or intended to be used in committing such depredation, or acquired by such depredation.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.127.title: Receiving property taken by war or depredation mentioned in sections 125 and 126

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Receiving property taken by war or depredation mentioned in sections 125 and 126: 127.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding receiving property taken by war or depredation mentioned in sections 125 and 126.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.127.full_text: 127. Whoever receives any property knowing the same to have been taken in the commission of any of the offences mentioned in sections 125 and 126, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine and to forfeiture of the property so received.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.128.title: Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of State or war to escape

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of State or war to escape: 128.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of state or war to escape.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.128.full_text: 128. Whoever, being a public servant and having the custody of any State prisoner or prisoner of war, voluntarily allows such prisoner to escape from any place in which such prisoner is confined, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.129.title: Public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape: 129.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.129.full_text:
129. Whoever, being a public servant and having the custody of any State prisoner or prisoner of war, negligently suffers such prisoner to escape from any place of confinement in
which such prisoner is confined, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.130.title: Aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner: 130.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.130.full_text:
130. Whoever knowingly aids or assists any State prisoner or prisoner of war in escaping from lawful custody, or rescues or attempts to rescue any such prisoner, or harbours or conceals any such prisoner who has escaped from lawful custody, or offers or attempts to offer any resistance to the recapture of such prisoner shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.-A State prisoner or prisoner of war, who is permitted to be at large on his parole within certain limits in Bangladesh, is said to escape from lawful custody if he goes beyond the limits within which he is allowed to be at large.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.131.title: Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty: 131.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.131.full_text:
131. Whoever abets the committing of mutiny by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of Bangladesh, or attempts to seduce any such officer, soldier, sailor or airman from his allegiance or his duty, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.-In this section the words "officer", “soldier", "sailor" and "airman" include any person subject to the Army Act, 1952 or the Navy Ordinance, 1961 or the Air Force Act, 1953, as the case may be.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.132.title: Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof: 132.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.132.full_text: 132. Whoever abets the committing of mutiny by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of Bangladesh, shall, if mutiny be committed in consequence of that abetment, be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.133.title: Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office: 133.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.133.full_text: 133. Whoever, abets an assault by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of Bangladesh, on any superior officer being in the execution of his office, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.134.title: Abetment of such assault, if the assault is committed

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abetment of such assault, if the assault is committed: 134.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abetment of such assault, if the assault is committed.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.134.full_text: 134. Whoever, abets an assault by an officer, soldier sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of Bangladesh, on any superior officer being in the execution of his office, shall, if such assault be committed in consequence of that abetment be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.135.title: Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman: 135.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.135.full_text: 135. Whoever abets the desertion of any officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of Bangladesh, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.136.title: Harbouring deserter

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Harbouring deserter: 136.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding harbouring deserter.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.136.full_text:
136. Whoever, except as hereinafter excepted, knowing or having reason to believe that an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of Bangladesh, has deserted, harbours such officer, soldier, sailor or airman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
Exception.-This provision does not extend to the case in which the harbour is given by a wife to her husband.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.137.title: Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master: 137.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.137.full_text: 137. The master or person in charge of a merchant vessel, on board of which any deserter from the Army, Navy or Air Force of Bangladesh is concealed, shall, though ignorant of such concealment, be liable to a penalty not exceeding five hundred taka if he might have known of such concealment but for some neglect of his duty as such master or person in charge, or but for some want of discipline on board of the vessel.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.138.title: Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman: 138.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.138.full_text: 138. Whoever abets what he knows to be an act of insubordination by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force of Bangladesh, shall, if such act of insubordination be committed in consequence of that abetment, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.139.title: Persons subject to certain acts

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Persons subject to certain acts: 139.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding persons subject to certain acts.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.139.full_text: 139. No person subject to the Army Act, 1952, the Navy Ordinance, 1961, the Air Force Act, 1953, is subject to punishment under this Code for any of the offences defined in this Chapter.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.140.title: Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman: 140.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.140.full_text: 140. Whoever, not being a soldier, sailor or airman in the Military, Naval or Air service of Bangladesh, wears any garb or carries any token resembling any garb or token used by such a soldier, sailor or airman with the intention that it may be believed that he is such a soldier, sailor or airman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred taka or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.141.title: Unlawful assembly

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Unlawful assembly: 141.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding unlawful assembly.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.141.full_text:
141. An assembly of five or more persons is designated an "unlawful assembly," if the common object of the persons composing that assembly is
First.-To overawe by criminal force, or show of criminal force, Government or Legislature, or any public servant in the exercise of the lawful power of such public servant; or
Second.-To resist the execution of any law, or of any legal process; or
Third.To commit any mischief or criminal trespass, or other offence; or
Fourth.-By means of criminal force, or show of criminal force, to any person to take or obtain possession of any property, or to deprive any person of the enjoyment of a right of way, or of the use of water or other incorporeal right of which he is in possession or enjoyment, or to enforce any right or supposed right; or
Fifth.-By means of criminal force, or show of criminal force, to compel any person to do what he is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do what he is legally entitled to do.
Explanation.-An assembly which was not unlawful when it assembled, may subsequently become an unlawful assembly.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.142.title: Being member of unlawful assembly

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Being member of unlawful assembly: 142.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding being member of unlawful assembly.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.142.full_text: 142. Whoever, being aware of facts which render any assembly an unlawful assembly, intentionally joins that assembly, or continues in it, is said to be a member of an unlawful assembly.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.143.title: Punishment

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment: 143.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.143.full_text: 143. Whoever is a member of an unlawful assembly, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.144.title: Joining unlawful assembly, armed with deadly weapon

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Joining unlawful assembly, armed with deadly weapon: 144.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding joining unlawful assembly, armed with deadly weapon.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.144.full_text: 144. Whoever, being armed with any deadly weapon, or with anything which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, is a member of an unlawful assembly, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.145.title: Joining or continuing in unlawful assembly, knowing it has been commanding to disperse

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Joining or continuing in unlawful assembly, knowing it has been commanding to disperse: 145.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding joining or continuing in unlawful assembly, knowing it has been commanding to disperse.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.145.full_text: 145. Whoever joins or continues in an unlawful assembly, knowing that such unlawful assembly has been commanded in the manner prescribed by law to disperse, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.146.title: Rioting

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Rioting: 146.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding rioting.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.146.full_text: 146. Whenever force or violence is used by an unlawful assembly, or by any member thereof, in prosecution of the common object of such assembly, every member of such assembly is guilty of the offence of rioting.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.147.title: Punishment for rioting

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment for rioting: 147.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment for rioting.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.147.full_text: 147. Whoever is guilty of rioting, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.148.title: Rioting, armed with deadly weapon

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Rioting, armed with deadly weapon: 148.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding rioting, armed with deadly weapon.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.148.full_text: 148. Whoever is guilty of rioting, being armed with a deadly weapon or with anything which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.149.title: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object: 149.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.149.full_text: 149. If an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object of that assembly, or such as the members of that assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object, every person who, at the time of the committing of that offence, is a member of the same assembly, is guilty of that offence.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.150.title: Hiring, or conniving at hiring, of persons to join unlawful assembly

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Hiring, or conniving at hiring, of persons to join unlawful assembly: 150.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding hiring, or conniving at hiring, of persons to join unlawful assembly.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.150.full_text: 150. Whoever hires or engages, or employs, or promotes, or connives at the hiring, engagement or employment of any person to join or become a member of any unlawful assembly, shall be punishable as a member of such unlawful assembly, and for any offence which may be committed by any such person as a member of such unlawful assembly in pursuance of such hiring, engagement or employment, in the same manner as if he had been a member of such unlawful assembly, or himself had committed such offence.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.151.title: Knowingly joining or continuing in assembly of five or more persons after it has been commanded to disperse

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Knowingly joining or continuing in assembly of five or more persons after it has been commanded to disperse: 151.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding knowingly joining or continuing in assembly of five or more persons after it has been commanded to disperse.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.151.full_text:
151. Whoever knowingly joins or continues in any assembly of five or more persons likely to cause a disturbance of the public peace, after such assembly has been lawfully commanded to disperse, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
Explanation.-If the assembly is an unlawful assembly within the meaning of section 141, the offender will be punishable under section 145.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.152.title: Assaulting or obstructing public servant when suppressing riot, etc.

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Assaulting or obstructing public servant when suppressing riot, etc.: 152.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding assaulting or obstructing public servant when suppressing riot, etc..
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.152.full_text: 152. Whoever assaults or threatens to assault, or obstructs or attempts to obstruct, any public servant in the discharge of his duty as such public servant, in endeavouring to disperse an unlawful assembly, or to suppress a riot or affray, or uses, or threatens, or attempts to use criminal force to such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.153.title: Wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot- if rioting be committed; if not committed

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot- if rioting be committed; if not committed: 153.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot- if rioting be committed; if not committed.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.153.full_text: 153. Whoever malignantly, or wantonly, by doing anything which is illegal, gives provocation to any person intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause the offence of rioting to be committed, shall, if the offence of rioting be committed in consequence of such provocation, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both; and if the offence of rioting be not committed, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.153A.title: Promoting enmity between classes

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Promoting enmity between classes: 153A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding promoting enmity between classes.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.153A.full_text:
153A. Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representations, or otherwise, promotes or attempts to promote feelings of enmity or hatred between different classes of the citizens of Bangladesh, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
Explanation.-It does not amount to an offence within the meaning of this section to point out, without malicious intention and with an honest view to their removal, matters which are producing or have a tendency to produce, feelings of enmity or hatred between different classes of the citizens of Bangladesh.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.153B.title: Inducing students, etc. to take part in political activity

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Inducing students, etc. to take part in political activity: 153B.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding inducing students, etc. to take part in political activity.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.153B.full_text: 153B. Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representations, or otherwise, induce or attempts to induce any student, or any class of students, or any institution interested in or connected with students, to take part in any political activity which disturbs or undermines, or is likely to disturb or undermine, the public order shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to two years or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.154.title: Owner or occupier of land on which an unlawful assembly is held

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Owner or occupier of land on which an unlawful assembly is held: 154.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding owner or occupier of land on which an unlawful assembly is held.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.154.full_text: 154. Whenever any unlawful assembly or riot takes place, the owner or occupier of the land upon which such unlawful assembly is held, or such riot is committed, and any person having or claiming an interest in such land, shall be punishable with fine not exceeding one thousand taka, if he or his agent or manager, knowing that such offence is being or has been committed, or having reason to believe it is likely to be committed, do not give the earliest notice thereof in his or their power to the principal officer at the nearest police-station, and do not, in the case of his or their having reason to believe that it was about to be committed, use all lawful means in his or their power to prevent it and, in the event of its taking place, do not use all lawful means in his or their power to disperse or suppress the riot or unlawful assembly.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.155.title: Liability of person for whose benefit riot is committed

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Liability of person for whose benefit riot is committed: 155.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding liability of person for whose benefit riot is committed.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.155.full_text: 155. Whenever a riot is committed for the benefit or on behalf of any person who is the owner or occupier of any land respecting which such riot takes place or who claims any interest in such land, or in the subject of any dispute which gave rise to the riot, or who has accepted or derived any benefit therefrom, such person shall be punishable with fine, if he or his agent or manager, having reason to believe that such riot was likely to be committed or that the unlawful assembly by which such riot was committed was likely to be held, shall not respectively use all lawful means in his or their power to prevent such assembly or riot from taking place, and for suppressing and dispersing the same.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.156.title: Liability of agent of owner or occupier for whose benefit riot is committed

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Liability of agent of owner or occupier for whose benefit riot is committed: 156.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding liability of agent of owner or occupier for whose benefit riot is committed.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.156.full_text:
156. Whenever a riot is committed for the benefit or on behalf of any person who is the owner or occupier of any land respecting which such riot takes place, or who claims any interest in such land, or in the subject of any dispute which gave rise to the riot, or who has accepted or derived any benefit therefrom,
the agent or manager of such person shall be punishable with fine, if such agent or manager, having reason to believe that such riot was likely to be committed, or that the unlawful assembly by which such riot was committed was likely to be held, shall not use all lawful means in his power to prevent such riot or assembly from taking place and for suppressing and dispersing the same.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.157.title: Harbouring persons hired for an unlawful assembly

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Harbouring persons hired for an unlawful assembly: 157.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding harbouring persons hired for an unlawful assembly.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.157.full_text: 157. Whoever harbours, receives or assembles, in any house or premises in his occupation or charge, or under his control any persons, knowing that such persons have been hired, engaged or employed, or are about to be hired, engaged or employed, to join or become members of an unlawful assembly, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.158.title: Being hired to take part in an unlawful assembly or riot; or to go armed

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Being hired to take part in an unlawful assembly or riot; or to go armed: 158.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding being hired to take part in an unlawful assembly or riot; or to go armed.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.158.full_text:
158. Whoever is engaged or hired, or offers or attempts to be hired or engaged, to do or assist in doing any of the acts specified in section 141, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
and whoever, being so engaged or hired as aforesaid, goes armed, or engages or offers to go armed, with any deadly weapon or with anything which used as a weapon of offence is likely to cause death, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.159.title: Affray

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Affray: 159.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding affray.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.159.full_text: 159. When two or more persons, by fighting in a public place, disturb the public peace, they are said to "commit an affray".

BD-PENAL-1860:s.160.title: Punishment for committing affray

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment for committing affray: 160.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment for committing affray.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.160.full_text: 160. Whoever commits an affray, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one hundred taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.161.title: Public servant taking gratification other than legal remuneration in respect of an official ac

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Public servant taking gratification other than legal remuneration in respect of an official ac: 161.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding public servant taking gratification other than legal remuneration in respect of an official ac.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.161.full_text:
161. Whoever, being or expecting to be a public servant, accepts or obtains, or agrees to accept, or attempts to obtain from any person, for himself or for any other person any gratification whatever, other than legal remuneration, as a motive or reward for doing or forbearing to do any official act or for showing or for bearing to show, in the exercise of his official functions, favour or disfavour to any person, or for rendering or attempting to render any service or disservice to any person, with the Government or Legislature, or with any public servant, as such, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
Explanations-“Expecting to be a public servant.” If a person not expecting to be in office obtains a gratification by deceiving others into a belief that he is about to be in office, and that he will then serve them, he may be guilty of cheating but he is not guilty of the offence defined in this section.
“Gratification.” The word “gratification” is not restricted to pecuniary gratifications, or to gratifications estimable in money.
“Legal remuneration.” The words “legal remuneration” are not restricted to remuneration which a public servant can lawfully demand, but include all remuneration which is permitted by the authority by which he is employed, to accept.
“A motive or reward for doing.” A person who receives a gratification as a motive for doing what he does not intend to do, or as a reward for doing what he has not done, comes within these words.
Illustrations
(a) A, a munsif, obtains from Z, a banker, a situation in Z's bank for A's brother, as a reward to A for deciding a cause in favour of Z. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
(b) A, holding the office of Consul at the Court of a foreign Power, accepts a lakh of taka from the Minister of that Power. It does not appear that A accepted this sum as a motive or reward for doing or forbearing to do any particular official act, or for rendering or attempting to render any particular service to that Power with the Government of Bangladesh. But it does appear that A accepted the sum as a motive or reward for generally showing favour in the exercise of his official functions to that Power. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
(c) A, a public servant, induces Z erroneously to believe that A's influence with Government has obtained a title for Z and thus induces Z to give A money as a reward for this service. A has committed the offence defined in this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.162.title: Taking gratification, in order, by corrupt or illegal means, to influence public servant

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Taking gratification, in order, by corrupt or illegal means, to influence public servant: 162.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding taking gratification, in order, by corrupt or illegal means, to influence public servant.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.162.full_text: 162. Whoever accepts or obtains, or agrees to accept, or attempts to obtain, from any person, for himself or for any other person, any gratification whatever as a motive or reward for inducing, by corrupt or illegal means, any public servant to do or to forbear to do any official act, or in the exercise of the official functions of such public servant to show favour or disfavour to any person, or to render or attempt to render any service or disservice to any person with the Government or Legislature, or with any public servant, as such, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.163.title: Taking gratification, for exercise of personal influence with public servant

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Taking gratification, for exercise of personal influence with public servant: 163.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding taking gratification, for exercise of personal influence with public servant.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.163.full_text:
163. Whoever accepts or obtains, or agrees to accept or attempts to obtain, from any person, for himself or for any other person, any gratification whatever, as a motive or reward for inducing, by the exercise of personal influence, any public servant to do or to forbear to do any official act, or in the exercise of the official functions of such public servant to show favour or disfavour to any person, or to render or attempt to render any service or disservice to any person with the Government or Legislature, or with any public servant, as such, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
Illustration
An advocate who receives a fee for arguing a case before a Judge; a person who receives pay for arranging and correcting a memorial addressed to Government, setting forth the services and claims of the memorialist; a paid agent for a condemned criminal, who lays before the Government statements tending to show that the condemnation was unjust, - are not within this section, inasmuch as they do not exercise or profess to exercise personal influence.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.164.title: Punishment for abetment by public servant of offences defined in section 162 or 163

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment for abetment by public servant of offences defined in section 162 or 163: 164.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment for abetment by public servant of offences defined in section 162 or 163.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.164.full_text:
164. Whoever, being a public servant, in respect of whom either of the offences defined in the last two preceding sections is committed, abets the offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
Illustration
A is a public servant. B, A's wife, receives a present as a motive for soliciting A to give an office to a particular person. A abets her doing so. B is punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year, or with fine, or with both. A is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.165A.title: Punishment for abetment of offences defined in sections 161 and 165

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment for abetment of offences defined in sections 161 and 165: 165A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment for abetment of offences defined in sections 161 and 165.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.165A.full_text: 165A. Whoever abets any offence punishable under section 161 or section 165 shall, whether the offence abetted is or is not committed in consequence of the abetment, be punished with the punishment provided for the offence.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.165B.title: Certain abettors excepted

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Certain abettors excepted: 165B.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding certain abettors excepted.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.165B.full_text: 165B. A person shall be deemed not to abet an offence punishable under section 161 or section 165 if he is induced, compelled, coerced, or intimidated to offer or give any such gratification as is referred to in section 161 for any of the purposes mentioned therein, or any valuable thing without consideration, or for an inadequate consideration, to any such public servant as is referred to in section 165.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.165.title: Public servant obtaining valuable thing, without consideration, from person concerned in proceeding or business transacted by such public servant

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Public servant obtaining valuable thing, without consideration, from person concerned in proceeding or business transacted by such public servant: 165.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding public servant obtaining valuable thing, without consideration, from person concerned in proceeding or business transacted by such public servant.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.165.full_text:
165. Whoever, being a public servant, accepts or obtains, or agrees to accept or attempts to obtain, for himself, or for any other person, any valuable thing without consideration, or for a consideration which he knows to be inadequate,
from any person whom he knows to have been, or to be, or to be likely to be concerned in any proceeding or business transacted or about to be transacted by such public servant, or having any connection with the official functions of himself or of any public servant to whom he is subordinate,
or from any person whom he knows to be interested in or related to the person so concerned,
shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
Illustrations
(a) A, a Collector, hires a house of Z, who has a settlement case pending before him. It is agreed that A shall pay fifty taka a month, the house being such that, if the bargain were made in good faith, A would be required to pay two hundred taka a month. A has obtained a valuable thing from Z without adequate consideration.
(b) A, a Judge, buys of Z, who has a case pending in A's Court, Government promissory notes at a discount, when they are selling in the market at a premium. A has obtained a valuable thing from Z without adequate consideration.
(c) Z's brother is apprehended and taken before A, a Magistrate, on a charge of perjury. A sells to Z shares in a bank at a premium, when they are selling in the market at a discount. Z pays A for the shares accordingly. The money so obtained by A is a valuable thing obtained by him without adequate consideration.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.166.title: Public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury to any person

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury to any person: 166.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury to any person.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.166.full_text:
166. Whoever, being a public servant, knowingly disobeys any direction of the law as to the way in which he is to conduct himself as such public servant, intending to cause, or knowing it to be likely that he will, by such disobedience, cause injury to any person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
Illustration
A, being an officer directed by law to take property in execution, in order to satisfy a decree pronounced in Z's favour by a Court of Justice, knowingly disobeys that direction of law, with the knowledge that he is likely thereby to cause injury to Z. A has committed the offence defined in this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.167.title: Public servant framing an incorrect document with intent to cause injury

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Public servant framing an incorrect document with intent to cause injury: 167.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding public servant framing an incorrect document with intent to cause injury.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.167.full_text: 167. Whoever, being a public servant, and being, as such public servant, charged with the preparation or translation of any document, frames or translates that document in a manner which he knows or believes to be incorrect, intending thereby to cause or knowing it to be likely that he may thereby cause injury to any person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.168.title: Public servant unlawfully engaging in trade

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Public servant unlawfully engaging in trade: 168.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding public servant unlawfully engaging in trade.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.168.full_text: 168. Whoever, being a public servant, and being legally bound as such public servant not to engage in trade, engages in trade, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.169.title: Public servant unlawfully buying or bidding for property

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Public servant unlawfully buying or bidding for property: 169.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding public servant unlawfully buying or bidding for property.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.169.full_text: 169. Whoever, being a public servant, and being legally bound as such public servant, not to purchase or bid for certain property, purchases or bids for that property, either in his own name or in the name of another, or jointly, or in shares with others, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both; and the property, if purchased, shall be confiscated.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.170.title: Personating a public servant

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Personating a public servant: 170.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding personating a public servant.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.170.full_text: 170. Whoever pretends to hold any particular office as a public servant, knowing that he does not hold such office or falsely personates any other person holding such office, and in such assumed character does or attempts to do any act under colour of such office, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description, for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171.title: Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent: 171.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding wearing garb or carrying token used by public servant with fraudulent intent.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171.full_text: 171. Whoever, not belonging to a certain class of public servants, wears any garb or carries any token resembling any garb or token used by that class of public servants, with the intention that it may be believed, or with the knowledge that it is likely to be believed, that he belongs to that class of public servants, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description, for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to two hundred taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171A.title: “Candidate”, “Electoral right” defined

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - “Candidate”, “Electoral right” defined: 171A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding “candidate”, “electoral right” defined.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171D.title: Personation at elections

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Personation at elections: 171D.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding personation at elections.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171D.full_text: 171D. Whoever at an election applies for a voting paper or votes in the name of any other person, whether living or dead, or in a fictitious name, or who having voted once at such election applies at the same election for a voting paper in his own name, and whoever abets, procures or attempts to procure the voting by any person in any such way, commits the offence of personation at an election.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171E.title: Punishment of bribery

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment of bribery: 171E.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment of bribery.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171E.full_text:
171E. Whoever commits the offence of bribery shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both:
Provided that bribery by treating shall be punished with fine only.
Explanation.-Treating means that form of bribery where the gratification consists in food, drink, entertainment, or provision.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171B.title: Bribery

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Bribery: 171B.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding bribery.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171B.full_text:
171B. (1) Whoever-
(i) gives a gratification to any person with the object of inducing him or any other person to exercise any electoral right or of rewarding any person for having exercised any such right; or
(ii) accepts either for himself or for any other person any gratification as a reward for exercising any such right or for inducing or attempting to induce any other person to exercise any such right,
commits the offence of bribery:
Provided that a declaration of public policy or a promise of public action shall not be an offence under this section.
(2) A person who offers, or agrees to give, or offers or attempts to procure, a gratification shall be deemed to give a gratification.
(3) A person who obtains or agrees to accept or attempts to obtain a gratification shall be deemed to accept a gratification, and a person who accepts a gratification as a motive for doing what he does not intend to do, or as a reward for doing what he has not done, shall be deemed to have accepted the gratification as a reward.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171C..title: Undue influence at elections

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Undue influence at elections: 171C.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding undue influence at elections.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171C..full_text:
171C.(1) Whoever voluntarily interferes or attempts to interfere with the free exercise of any electoral right commits the offence of undue influence at an election.
(2) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions of sub-section (1), whoever
(a) threatens any candidate or voter, or any person in whom a candidate or voter is interested, with injury of any kind, or
(b) induces or attempts to induce a candidate or voter to believe that he or any person in whom he is interested will become or will be rendered an object of Divine displeasure or of spiritual censure,
shall be deemed to interfere with the free exercise of the electoral right of such candidate or voter, within the meaning of sub-section (1).
(3) A declaration of public policy or a promise of public action, or the mere exercise of a legal right without intent to interfere with an electoral right, shall not be deemed to be interference within the meaning of this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171F.title: Punishment for undue influence or personation at an election

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment for undue influence or personation at an election: 171F.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment for undue influence or personation at an election.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171F.full_text: 171F. Whoever commits the offence of undue influence of personation at an election shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171G.title: False statement in connection with an election

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - False statement in connection with an election: 171G.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding false statement in connection with an election.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171G.full_text: 171G. Whoever with intent to affect the result of an election makes or publishes any statement purporting to be a statement of fact which is false and which he either knows or believes to be or does not believe to be true, in relation to the personal character or conduct of any candidate shall be punished with fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171H.title: Illegal payments in connection with an election

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Illegal payments in connection with an election: 171H.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding illegal payments in connection with an election.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.171H.full_text:
171H. Whoever without the general or special authority in writing of a candidate incurs or authorises expenses on account of the holding of any public meeting, or upon any advertisement, circular or publication, or in any other way whatsoever for the purpose of promoting or procuring the election of such candidate, shall be punished with fine which may extend to five hundred taka:
