exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.240.full_text: 240. Whoever, having any counterfeit coin, which is a counterfeit of Bangladesh coin, and which, at the time when he became possessed of it, he knew to be a counterfeit of Bangladesh coin, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, delivers the same to any person, or attempts to induce any person to receive it, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.241.title: Delivery of coin as genuine, which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be counterfeit

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Delivery of coin as genuine, which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be counterfeit: 241.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding delivery of coin as genuine, which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be counterfeit.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.241.full_text:
241. Whoever delivers to any other person as genuine, or attempts to induce any other person to receive as genuine, any counterfeit coin which he knows to be counterfeit, but which he did not know to be counterfeit at the time when he took it into his possession, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine to an amount which may extend is ten times the value of the coin counterfeited, or with both.
Illustration
A, a coiner, delivers counterfeit Company's taka to his accomplice B, for the purpose of uttering them. B sells the taka to C, another, utterer, who buys them knowing them to be counterfeit. C pays away the taka for goods to D, who receives them, not knowing them to be counterfeit. D after receiving the taka, discovers that they are counterfeit and pays them away as if they were good. Here D is punishable only under this section, but B and C are punishable under section 239 or 240, as the case may be.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.242.title: Possession of counterfeit coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Possession of counterfeit coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof: 242.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding possession of counterfeit coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.242.full_text: 242. Whoever, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, is in possession of counterfeit coin, having known at the time when he became possessed thereof that such coin was counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.243.title: Possession of Bangladesh coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Possession of Bangladesh coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof: 243.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding possession of bangladesh coin by person who knew it to be counterfeit when he became possessed thereof.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.243.full_text: 243. Whoever, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, is in possession of counterfeit coin, which is a counterfeit of Bangladesh coin, having known at the time when he became possessed of it that it was counterfeit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.244.title: Person employed in mint causing coin to be of different weight or composition from that fixed by law

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Person employed in mint causing coin to be of different weight or composition from that fixed by law: 244.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding person employed in mint causing coin to be of different weight or composition from that fixed by law.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.244.full_text: 244. Whoever, being employed in any mint lawfully established in Bangladesh, does any act, or omits what he is legally bound to do, with the intention of causing any coin issued from that mint to be of a different weight or composition from the weight or composition fixed by law, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.245.title: Unlawfully taking coining instrument from mint

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Unlawfully taking coining instrument from mint: 245.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding unlawfully taking coining instrument from mint.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.245.full_text: 245. Whoever, without lawful authority, takes out of any mint, lawfully established in Bangladesh, any coining tool or instrument, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.246.title: Fraudulently or dishonesty diminishing weight or altering composition of coin

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Fraudulently or dishonesty diminishing weight or altering composition of coin: 246.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding fraudulently or dishonesty diminishing weight or altering composition of coin.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.246.full_text:
246. Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly performs on any coin any operation which diminishes the weight or alters the composition of that coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.-A person who scoops out part of the coin and puts anything else into the cavity alters the composition of that coin.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.247.title: Fraudulently or dishonestly diminishing weight or altering composition of Bangladesh coin

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Fraudulently or dishonestly diminishing weight or altering composition of Bangladesh coin: 247.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding fraudulently or dishonestly diminishing weight or altering composition of bangladesh coin.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.247.full_text: 247. Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly performs on any Bangladesh coin, any operation which diminishes the weight or alters the composition of that coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.248.title: Altering appearance of coin with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Altering appearance of coin with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description: 248.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding altering appearance of coin with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.248.full_text: 248. Whoever performs on any coin any operation which alters the appearance of that coin, with the intention that the said coin shall pass as a coin of a different description, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.249.title: Altering appearance of Bangladesh coin, with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Altering appearance of Bangladesh coin, with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description: 249.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding altering appearance of bangladesh coin, with intent that it shall pass as coin of different description.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.249.full_text: 249. Whoever performs on any Bangladesh coin any operation which alters the appearance of that coin, with the intention that the said coin shall pass as a coin of a different description, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.250.title: Delivery of coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Delivery of coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered: 250.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding delivery of coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.250.full_text: 250. Whoever, having coin in his possession with respect to which the offence defined in section 246 or 248 has been committed, and having known at the time when he became possessed of such coin that such offence had been committed with respect to it, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, delivers such coin to any other person, or attempts to induce any other person to receive the same, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.251.title: Delivery of Bangladesh coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Delivery of Bangladesh coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered: 251.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding delivery of bangladesh coin, possessed with knowledge that it is altered.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.251.full_text: 251. Whoever, having coin in his possession with respect to which the offence defined in section 247 or 249 has been committed, and having known at the time when he became possessed of such coin that such offence had been committed with respect to it, fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, delivers such coin to any other person, or attempts to induce any other person to receive the same, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.252.title: Possession of coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Possession of coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof: 252.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding possession of coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.252.full_text: 252. Whoever fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, is in possession of coin with respect to which the offence defined in either of the section 246 or 248 has been committed, having known at the time of becoming possessed thereof that such offence had been committed with respect to such coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.253.title: Possession of Bangladesh coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Possession of Bangladesh coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof: 253.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding possession of bangladesh coin by person who knew it to be altered when he became possessed thereof.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.253.full_text: 253. Whoever fraudulently or with intent that fraud may be committed, is in possession of coin with respect to which the offence defined in either of the section 247 or 249 has been committed having known at the time of becoming possessed thereof, that such offence had been committed with respect to such coin, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.254.title: Delivery of coin as genuine which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be altered

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Delivery of coin as genuine which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be altered: 254.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding delivery of coin as genuine which, when first possessed, the deliverer did not know to be altered.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.254.full_text: 254. Whoever delivers to any other person as genuine or as a coin of a different description from what it is, or attempts to induce any person to receive as genuine, or as a different coin from what it is, any coin in respect of which he knows that any such operation as that mentioned in sections 246, 247, 248, or 249 has been performed, but in respect of which he did not, at the time when he took it into his possession, know that such operation had been performed, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine to an amount which may extend to ten times the value of the coin for which the altered coin is passed, or attempted to be passed.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.255.title: Counterfeiting Government stamp

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Counterfeiting Government stamp: 255.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding counterfeiting government stamp.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.255.full_text:
255. Whoever counterfeits or knowingly performs any part of the process of counterfeiting, any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, shall be punished with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.-A person commits this offence who counterfeits by causing a genuine stamp of one denomination to appear like a genuine stamp of a different denomination.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.256.title: Having possession of instrument or material for counterfeiting Government stamp

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Having possession of instrument or material for counterfeiting Government stamp: 256.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding having possession of instrument or material for counterfeiting government stamp.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.256.full_text: 256. Whoever has in his possession any instrument or material for the purpose of being used, or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used, for the purpose of counterfeiting any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.257.title: Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting Government stamp

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Making or selling instrument for counterfeiting Government stamp: 257.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding making or selling instrument for counterfeiting government stamp.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.257.full_text: 257. Whoever makes or performs any part of the process of making, or buys, or sells, or disposes of, any instrument for the purpose of being used, or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used, for the purpose of counterfeiting any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.258.title: Sale of counterfeit Government stamp

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Sale of counterfeit Government stamp: 258.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding sale of counterfeit government stamp.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.258.full_text: 258. Whoever sells, or offers for sale, any stamp which he knows or has reason to believe to be a counterfeit of any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.259.title: Having possession of counterfeit Government stamp

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Having possession of counterfeit Government stamp: 259.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding having possession of counterfeit government stamp.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.259.full_text: 259. Whoever has in his possession any stamp which he knows to be a counterfeit of any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, intending to use, or dispose of the same as a genuine stamp, or in order that it may be used as a genuine stamp, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.260.title: Using as genuine a Government stamp known to be counterfeit

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Using as genuine a Government stamp known to be counterfeit: 260.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding using as genuine a government stamp known to be counterfeit.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.260.full_text: 260. Whoever uses as genuine any stamp, knowing it to be a counterfeit of any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.261.title: Effacing writing from substance bearing Government stamp, or removing from document a stamp used for it, with intent to cause loss to Government

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Effacing writing from substance bearing Government stamp, or removing from document a stamp used for it, with intent to cause loss to Government: 261.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding effacing writing from substance bearing government stamp, or removing from document a stamp used for it, with intent to cause loss to government.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.261.full_text: 261. Whoever fraudulently or with intent to cause loss to the Government, removes or effaces from any substance, bearing any stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, any writing or document for which such stamp has been used, or removes from any writing or document a stamp which has been used for such writing or document, in order that such stamp may be used for a different writing or document, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.262.title: Using Government stamp known to have been before used

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Using Government stamp known to have been before used: 262.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding using government stamp known to have been before used.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.262.full_text: 262. Whoever fraudulently or with intent to cause loss to the Government, uses for any purpose a stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, which he knows to have been before used, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.263.title: Erasure of mark denoting that stamp has been used

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Erasure of mark denoting that stamp has been used: 263.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding erasure of mark denoting that stamp has been used.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.263.full_text: 263. Whoever fraudulently or with intent to cause loss to Government, erases or removes from a stamp issued by Government for the purpose of revenue, any mark, put or impressed upon such stamp for the purpose of denoting that the same has been used, or knowingly has in his possession or sells or disposes of any such stamp from which such mark has been erased or removed, or sells or disposes of any such stamp which he knows to have been used, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.263A.title: Prohibition of fictitious stamps

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Prohibition of fictitious stamps: 263A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding prohibition of fictitious stamps.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.263A.full_text:
263A. (1) Whoever
(a) makes, knowingly utters, deals in or sells any fictitious stamp, or knowingly uses for any postal purpose any fictitious stamp, or
(b) has in his possession, without lawful excuse, any fictitious stamp, or
(c) makes or, without lawful excuse, has in his possession any die, plate, instrument or materials for making any fictitious stamp,
shall be punished with fine which may extend to two hundred taka.
(2) Any such stamp, die, plate, instrument or materials in the possession of any person for making any fictitious stamp may be seized and shall be forfeited.
(3) In this section “fictitious stamp" means any stamp falsely purporting to be issued by Government for the purpose of denoting a rate of postage or any facsimile or imitation or representation, whether on paper or otherwise, of any stamp issued by Government for that purpose.
(4) In this section and also in sections 255 to 263, both inclusive, the word “Government" when used in connection with, or in reference to, any stamp issued for the purpose of denoting a rate of postage, shall, notwithstanding anything in section 17, be deemed to include the person or persons authorized by law to administer executive government in any part of Bangladesh, and also in any part of Her Majesty's dominions or in any foreign country.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.264.title: Fraudulent use of false instrument for weighing

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Fraudulent use of false instrument for weighing: 264.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding fraudulent use of false instrument for weighing.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.264.full_text: 264. Whoever fraudulently uses any instrument for weighing which he knows to be false, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.265.title: Fraudulent use of false weight or measure

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Fraudulent use of false weight or measure: 265.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding fraudulent use of false weight or measure.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.265.full_text: 265. Whoever fraudulently uses any false weight or false measure of length or capacity, or fraudulently uses any weight or any measure of length or capacity as a different weight or measure from what it is, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.266.title: Being in possession of false weight or measure

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Being in possession of false weight or measure: 266.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding being in possession of false weight or measure.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.266.full_text: 266. Whoever is in possession of any instrument for weighing, or of any weight, or of any measure of length or capacity, which he knows to be false, and intending that the same may be fraudulently used, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.267.title: Making or selling false weight or measure

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Making or selling false weight or measure: 267.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding making or selling false weight or measure.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.267.full_text: 267. Whoever makes, sells or disposes of any instrument for weighing, or any weight, or any measure of length or capacity which he knows to be false, in order that the same may be used as true, or knowing that the same is likely to be used as true, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.268.title: Public nuisance

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Public nuisance: 268.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding public nuisance.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.268.full_text: 268. A person is guilty of a public nuisance who does any act or is guilty of an illegal omission which causes any common injury, danger or annoyance to the public or to the people in general who dwell or occupy property in the vicinity, or which must necessarily cause injury, obstruction, dangers or annoyance to persons who may have occasion to use any public right.A common nuisance is not excused on the ground that it causes some convenience or advantage.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.269.title: Negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life: 269.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.269.full_text: 269. Whoever unlawfully or negligently does any act which is, and which he knows or has reason to believe to be, likely to spread the infection of any disease dangerous to life, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.270.title: Malignant act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Malignant act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life: 270.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding malignant act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.270.full_text: 270. Whoever malignantly does any act which is, and which he knows or has reason to believe to be, likely to spread the infection of any disease dangerous to life, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.271.title: Disobedience to quarantine rule

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Disobedience to quarantine rule: 271.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding disobedience to quarantine rule.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.271.full_text: 271. Whoever knowingly disobeys any rule made and promulgated by the Government for putting any vessel into a state of quarantine, or for regulating the intercourse of vessels in a state of quarantine with the shore or with other vessels, or for regulating the intercourse between places where an infectious disease prevails and other places, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.272.title: Adulteration of food or drink intended for sale

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Adulteration of food or drink intended for sale: 272.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding adulteration of food or drink intended for sale.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.272.full_text: 272. Whoever adulterates any article of food or drink, so as to make such article noxious as food or drink, intending to sell such article as food or drink, or knowing it to be likely that the same will be sold as food or drink, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.273.title: Sale of noxious food or drink

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Sale of noxious food or drink: 273.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding sale of noxious food or drink.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.273.full_text: 273. Whoever sells, or offers or exposes for sale, as food or drink, any article which has been rendered or has become noxious, or is in a state unfit for food or drink, knowing or having reason to believe that the same is noxious as food or drink, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.274.title: Adulteration of drugs

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Adulteration of drugs: 274.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding adulteration of drugs.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.274.full_text: 274. Whoever adulterates any drug or medical preparation in such a manner as to lessen the efficacy or change the operation of such drug or medical preparation, or to make it noxious, intending that it shall be sold or used for, or knowing it to be likely that it will be sold or used for, any medicinal purpose, as if it had not undergone such adulteration, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.275.title: Sale of adulterated drugs

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Sale of adulterated drugs: 275.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding sale of adulterated drugs.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.275.full_text: 275. Whoever, knowing any drug or medical preparation to have been adulterated in such a manner as to lessen its efficacy, to change its operation, or to render it noxious, sells the same, or offers or exposes it for sale, or issues it from any dispensary for medicinal purposes as unadulterated, or causes it to be used for medicinal purposes by any person not knowing of the adulteration, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.276.title: Sale of drug as a different drug or preparation

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Sale of drug as a different drug or preparation: 276.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding sale of drug as a different drug or preparation.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.276.full_text: 276. Whoever knowingly sells, or offers or exposes for sale, or issues from a dispensary for medicinal purposes, any drug or medicinal preparation, as a different drug or medical preparation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.277.title: Fouling water or public spring or reservoir

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Fouling water or public spring or reservoir: 277.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding fouling water or public spring or reservoir.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.277.full_text: 277. Whoever voluntarily corrupts or fouls the water of any public spring or reservoir, so as to render it less fit for the purpose for which it is ordinarily used, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred taka or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.278.title: Making atmosphere noxious to health

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Making atmosphere noxious to health: 278.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding making atmosphere noxious to health.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.278.full_text: 278. Whoever voluntarily vitiates the atmosphere in any place so as to make it noxious to the health of persons in general dwelling or carrying on business in the neighborhood or passing along a public way, shall be punished with fine which may extend to five hundred taka.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.279.title: Rash driving or riding on a public way

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Rash driving or riding on a public way: 279.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding rash driving or riding on a public way.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.279.full_text:
279. Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may, subject to the minimum of one thousand taka, extend to five thousand taka or with both.
 
Explanation. Any person driving any vehicle, or riding, on any public way, in a speed which exceeds the limit prescribed in this behalf by or under any law for the time being in force shall, for the purpose of this section, be deemed to have driven so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or cause hurt or injury to any other person.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.280.title: Rash navigation of vessel

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Rash navigation of vessel: 280.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding rash navigation of vessel.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.280.full_text: 280. Whoever navigates any vessel in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.281.title: Exhibition of false light, mark or buoy

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Exhibition of false light, mark or buoy: 281.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding exhibition of false light, mark or buoy.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.281.full_text: 281. Whoever exhibits any false light, mark or buoy, intending or knowing it to be likely that such exhibition will mislead any navigator, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.282.title: Conveying person by water for hire in unsafe or over-loaded vessel

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Conveying person by water for hire in unsafe or over-loaded vessel: 282.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding conveying person by water for hire in unsafe or over-loaded vessel.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.282.full_text: 282. Whoever knowingly or negligently conveys, or causes to be conveyed for, hire, any person by water in any vessel, when that vessel is in such a state or so loaded as to endanger the life of that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.283.title: Danger or obstruction in public way or line of navigation

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Danger or obstruction in public way or line of navigation: 283.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding danger or obstruction in public way or line of navigation.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.283.full_text: 283. Whoever, by doing any act, or by omitting to take order with any property in his possession or under his charge, causes danger, obstruction or injury to any person in any public way or public line of navigation, shall be punished with fine which may extend to two hundred taka.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.284.title: Negligent conduct with respect to poisonous substance

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Negligent conduct with respect to poisonous substance: 284.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding negligent conduct with respect to poisonous substance.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.284.full_text:
284. Whoever does, with any poisonous substance, any act in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any person,
or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any poisonous substance in his possession as is sufficient to guard against probable danger to human life from such poisonous substance,
shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.285.title: Negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter: 285.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.285.full_text:
285. Whoever does, with fire or any combustible matter, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person,
or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any fire or any combustible matter in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from such fire or combustible matter,
shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.286.title: Negligent conduct with respect to explosive substance

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Negligent conduct with respect to explosive substance: 286.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding negligent conduct with respect to explosive substance.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.286.full_text:
286. Whoever does, with any explosive substance, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person,
or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any explosive substance in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from that substance,
shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.287.title: Negligent conduct with respect to machinery

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Negligent conduct with respect to machinery: 287.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding negligent conduct with respect to machinery.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.287.full_text:
287. Whoever does, with any machinery, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person,
or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any machinery in his possession or under his care as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from such machinery,
shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.288.title: Negligent conduct with respect to pulling down or repairing buildings

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Negligent conduct with respect to pulling down or repairing buildings: 288.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding negligent conduct with respect to pulling down or repairing buildings.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.288.full_text: 288. Whoever, in pulling down or repairing any building, knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with that building as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from the fall of that building, or of any part thereof, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.289.title: Negligent conduct with respect to animal

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Negligent conduct with respect to animal: 289.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding negligent conduct with respect to animal.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.289.full_text: 289. Whoever knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any animal in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life, or any probable danger of grievous hurt from such animal, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand taka, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.290.title: Punishment for public nuisance in cases not otherwise provided for

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment for public nuisance in cases not otherwise provided for: 290.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment for public nuisance in cases not otherwise provided for.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.290.full_text: 290. Whoever commits a public nuisance in any case not otherwise punishable by this Code, shall be punished with fine which may extend to two hundred taka.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.291.title: Continuance of nuisance after injunction to discontinue

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Continuance of nuisance after injunction to discontinue: 291.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding continuance of nuisance after injunction to discontinue.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.291.full_text: 291. Whoever repeats or continues a public nuisance, having been enjoined by any public servant who has lawful authority to issue such injunction not to repeat or continue such nuisance, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.292.title: Sale, etc., of obscene books, etc.

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Sale, etc., of obscene books, etc.: 292.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding sale, etc., of obscene books, etc..
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.292.full_text:
292. Whoever
(a) sells, lets to hire, distributes, publicly exhibits or in any manner puts into circulation, or for purposes of sale, hire, distribution, public exhibition or circulation, makes, produces or has in his possession any obscene book, pamphlet, paper, drawing, painting, representation or figure or any other obscene object whatsoever, or
(b) imports, exports or conveys any obscene object for any of the purposes aforesaid, or knowing or having reason to believe that such object will be sold, let to hire, distributed or publicly exhibited or in any manner put into circulation, or
(c) takes part in or receives profits from any business in the course of which he knows or has reason to believe that any such obscene objects are, for any of the purposes aforesaid, made, produced, purchased, kept, imported, exported, conveyed, publicly exhibited or in any manner put into circulation, or
(d) advertises or makes known by any means whatsoever that any person is engaged or is ready to engage in any act which is an offence under this section, or that any such obscene object can be procured from or through any person, or
(e) offers or attempts to do any act which is an offence under this section,
shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both.
Exception.- This section does not extend to any book, pamphlet, writing, drawing or painting kept or used bona fide for religious purposes or any representation sculptured, engraved, painted or otherwise represented on or in any temple, or on any car used for the conveyance of idols, or kept or used for any religious purpose.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.293.title: Sale, etc., of obscene objects to young person

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Sale, etc., of obscene objects to young person: 293.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding sale, etc., of obscene objects to young person.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.293.full_text: 293. Whoever sells, lets to hire, distributes, exhibits or circulates to any person under the age of twenty years any such obscene object as is referred to in the last preceding section, or offers or attempts so to do, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.294.title: Obscene acts and songs

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Obscene acts and songs: 294.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding obscene acts and songs.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.294.full_text:
294. Whoever, to the annoyance of others,
(a) does any obscene act in any public place, or
(b) sings, recites or utters any obscene songs, ballad or words, in or near any public place,
shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.294A.title: Keeping lottery-office

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Keeping lottery-office: 294A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding keeping lottery-office.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.294A.full_text:
294A. Whoever keeps any office or place for the purpose of drawing any lottery not being a State lottery or a lottery authorized by the Government shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
And whoever publishes any proposal to pay any sum, or to deliver any goods, or to do or forbear doing anything for the benefit of any person, on any event or contingency relative or applicable to the drawing of any ticket, lot, number or figure in any such lottery shall be punished with fine which may extend to one thousand taka.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.294B.title: Offering of prize in connection with trade, etc.

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Offering of prize in connection with trade, etc.: 294B.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding offering of prize in connection with trade, etc..
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.294B.full_text: 294B. Whoever offers, or undertakes to offer, in connection with any trade or business or sale of any commodity, any prize, reward or other similar consideration, by whatever name called, whether in money or kind, against any coupon, ticket, number or figure, or by any other device, as an inducement or encouragement to trade or business or to the buying of any commodity, or for the purpose of advertisement or popularising any commodity, and whoever publishes any such offer, shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.295.title: Injuring or defiling place of worship, with intent to insult the religion of any class

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Injuring or defiling place of worship, with intent to insult the religion of any class: 295.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding injuring or defiling place of worship, with intent to insult the religion of any class.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.295.full_text: 295. Whoever destroys, damages or defiles any place of worship, or any object held sacred by any class of persons with the intention of thereby insulting the religion of any class of persons or with the knowledge that any class of persons is likely to consider such destruction, damage or defilement as an insult to their religion, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.295A.title: Deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs: 295A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.295A.full_text: 295A. Whoever, with deliberate and malicious intention of outraging the religious feelings of any class of the citizens of Bangladesh, by words, either spoken or written, or by visible representations insults or attempts to insult the religion or the religious beliefs of that class, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.296.title: Disturbing religious assembly

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Disturbing religious assembly: 296.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding disturbing religious assembly.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.296.full_text: 296. Whoever voluntarily causes disturbance to any assembly lawfully engaged in the performance of religious worship, or religious ceremonies, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.297.title: Trespassing on burial places, etc.

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Trespassing on burial places, etc.: 297.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding trespassing on burial places, etc..
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.297.full_text:
297. Whoever, with the intention of wounding the feelings of any person, or of insulting the religion of any person, or with the knowledge that the feelings of any person are likely to be wounded, or that the religion of any person is likely to be insulted thereby,
commits any trespass in any place of worship or on any place of sepulture, or any place set apart for the performance of funeral rites or as a depository for the remains of the dead, or offers any indignity to any human corpse, or causes disturbance to any persons assembled for the performance of funeral ceremonies,
shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.298.title: Uttering words, etc., with deliberate intent to wound religious feelings

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Uttering words, etc., with deliberate intent to wound religious feelings: 298.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding uttering words, etc., with deliberate intent to wound religious feelings.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.298.full_text: 298. Whoever, with the deliberate intention of wounding the religious feelings of any person, utters any word or makes any sound in the hearing of that person or makes any gesture in the sight of that person or places any object in the sight of that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.299.title: Culpable homicide

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Culpable homicide: 299.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding culpable homicide.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.299.full_text:
299. Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of culpable homicide.
Illustrations
(a) A lays sticks and turf over a pit, with the intention of thereby causing death, or with the knowledge that death is likely to be thereby caused. Z, believing the ground to be firm, treads on it, falls in and is killed. A has committed the offence of culpable homicide.
(b) A knows Z to be behind a bush. B does not know it. A, intending to cause, or knowing it to be likely to cause Z's death induces B to fire at the bush. B fires and kills Z. Here B may be guilty of no offence; but A has committed the offence of culpable homicide.
(c) A, by shooting at a fowl with intent to kill and steal it, kills B, who is behind a bush; A not knowing that he was there. Here, although A was doing an unlawful act, he was not guilty of culpable homicide, as he did not intend to kill B or cause death by doing an act that he knew was likely to cause death.
Explanation 1. A person who causes bodily injury to another who is labouring under a disorder, disease or bodily infirmity, and thereby accelerates the death of that other, shall be deemed to have caused his death.
Explanation 2. Where death is caused by bodily injury, the person who causes such bodily injury shall be deemed to have caused the death, although by resorting to proper remedies and skilful treatment the death might have been prevented.
Explanation 3. The causing of the death of a child in the mother's womb is not homicide. But it may amount to culpable homicide to cause the death of a living child, if any part of that child has been brought forth, though the child may not have breathed or been completely born.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.300.title: Murder

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Murder: 300.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding murder.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.300.full_text:
300. Except in the cases hereinafter excepted, culpable homicide is murder, if the act by which the death is caused is done with the intention of causing death, or-
Secondly.-If it is done with the intention of causing such bodily injury as the offender knows to be likely to cause the death of the person to whom the harm is caused, or –
Thirdly.-If it is done with the intention of causing bodily injury to any person and the bodily injury intended to be inflicted is sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death, or –
Fourthly.--f the person committing the act knows that it is so imminently dangerous that it must, in all probability, cause death, or such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, and commits such act without any excuse for incurring the risk of causing death or such injury as aforesaid.
Illustrations
(a) A shoots Z with the intention of killing him. Z dies in consequence. A commits murder.
(b) A, knowing that Z is labouring under such a disease that a blow is likely to cause his death, strikes him with the intention of causing bodily injury. Z dies in consequence of the blow. A is guilty of murder, although the blow might not have been sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause the death of a person in a sound state of health. But if A, not knowing that Z is labouring under any disease, gives him such a blow as would not in the ordinary course of nature kill a person in a sound state of health, here A, although he may intend to cause bodily injury, is not guilty of murder, if he did not intend to cause death or such bodily injury as in the ordinary course of nature would cause death.
(c) A intentionally gives Z a sword-cut or club-wound sufficient to cause the death of a man in the ordinary course of nature. Z dies in consequence. Here A is guilty of murder, although he may not have intended to cause Z's death.
(d) A without any excuse fires a loaded cannon into a crowd of persons and kills one of them. A is guilty of murder, although he may not have had a premeditated design to kill any particular individual.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.301.title: Culpable homicide by causing death of person other than person whose death was intended

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Culpable homicide by causing death of person other than person whose death was intended: 301.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding culpable homicide by causing death of person other than person whose death was intended.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.301.full_text: 301. If a person, by doing anything which he intends or knows to be likely to cause death, commits culpable homicide by causing the death of any person, whose death he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause, the culpable homicide committed by the offender is of the description of which it would have been if he had caused the death of the person whose death he intended or knew himself to be likely to cause.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.302.title: Punishment for murder

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment for murder: 302.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment for murder.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.302.full_text: 302. Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.303.title: Punishment for murder by life-convict

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment for murder by life-convict: 303.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment for murder by life-convict.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.303.full_text: 303. Whoever, being under sentence of imprisonment for life, commits murder, shall be punished with death.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.304A.title: Causing death by negligence

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Causing death by negligence: 304A.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding causing death by negligence.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.304A.full_text: 304A. Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.304B.title: Causing death by rash driving or riding on a public way

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Causing death by rash driving or riding on a public way: 304B.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding causing death by rash driving or riding on a public way.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.304B.full_text: 304B. Whoever causes the death of any person by rash or negligent driving of any vehicle or riding on any public way not amounting to culpable homicide shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.304.title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder: 304.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.304.full_text:
304. Whoever commits culpable homicide not amounting to murder, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine, if the act by which the death is caused is done with intention of causing death, or of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death;
or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, or with fine, or with both, if the act is done with the knowledge that it is likely to cause death, but without any intention to cause death or to cause such bodily injury as is likely to cause death.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.305.title: Abetment of suicide of child or insane person

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abetment of suicide of child or insane person: 305.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abetment of suicide of child or insane person.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.305.full_text:
305. If any person under eighteen years of age, any insane person, any delirious person, any idiot, or any person in a state of intoxication commits suicide, whoever abets the commission
of such suicide shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.306.title: Abetment of suicide

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Abetment of suicide: 306.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding abetment of suicide.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.306.full_text: 306. If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.307.title: Attempt to murder Attempts by life-convicts

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Attempt to murder Attempts by life-convicts: 307.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding attempt to murder attempts by life-convicts.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.307.full_text:
307. Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and, if hurt is caused to any person by such act, the offender shall be liable either to imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned.
When any person offending under this section is under sentence of imprisonment for life, he may, if hurt is caused, be punished with death.
Illustration
(a) A shoots at Z with intention to kill him, under such circumstances that, if death ensued, A would be guilty of murder. A is liable to punishment under this section.
(b) A with the intention of causing the death of a child of tender years exposes it in a desert place. A has committed the offence defined by this section, though the death of the child does not ensue.
(c) A, intending to murder Z, buys a gun and loads it. A has not yet committed the offence. A fires the gun at Z. He has committed the offence defined in this section, and, if by such firing he wounds, he is liable to the punishment provided by the latter part of the first paragraph of this section.
(d) A, intending to murder Z, by poison, purchases poison and mixes the same with food which remains in A's keeping; A has not yet committed the offence in this section. A places the food on Z's table or delivers it to Z's servants to place it on Z's table. A has committed the offence defined in this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.308.title: Attempt to commit culpable homicide

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Attempt to commit culpable homicide: 308.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding attempt to commit culpable homicide.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.308.full_text:
308. Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and, if hurt is caused to any person by such act, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
Illustration
A, on grave and sudden provocation, fires a pistol at Z, under such circumstances that if he thereby caused death he would be guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. A has committed the offence defined in this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.309.title: Attempt to commit suicide

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Attempt to commit suicide: 309.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding attempt to commit suicide.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.309.full_text: 309. Whoever attempts to commit suicide and does any act towards the commission of such offence, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.310.title: Thug

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Thug: 310.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding thug.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.310.full_text: 310. Whoever, at any time after the passing of this Act, shall have been habitually associated with any other or others for the purpose of committing robbery or child-stealing by means of or accompanied with murder, is a thug.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.311.title: Punishment

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Punishment: 311.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding punishment.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.311.full_text: 311. Whoever is a thug, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.312.title: Causing miscarriage

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Causing miscarriage: 312.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding causing miscarriage.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.312.full_text:
312. Whoever voluntarily causes a woman with child to miscarry, shall, if such miscarriage be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the woman, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and, if the woman be quick with child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.-A woman who causes herself to miscarry, is within the meaning of this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.313.title: Causing miscarriage without women's consent

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Causing miscarriage without women's consent: 313.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding causing miscarriage without women's consent.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.313.full_text: 313. Whoever commits the offence defined in the last preceding section without the consent of the woman, whether the woman is quick with child or not, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.314.title: Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage: 314.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.314.full_text:
314. Whoever, with intent to cause the miscarriage of a woman with child, does any act which causes the death of such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description
for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine,

BD-PENAL-1860:s.315.title: Act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause it to die after birth

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause it to die after birth: 315.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause it to die after birth.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.315.full_text: 315. Whoever before the birth of any child does any act with the intention of thereby preventing that child from being born alive or causing it to die after its birth, and does by such act prevent that child from being born alive, or causes it to die after its birth, shall, if such act be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the mother, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.316.title: Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide: 316.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.316.full_text:
316. Whoever does any act under such circumstances, that if he thereby caused death he would be guilty of culpable homicide, and does by such act cause the death of a quick unborn child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Illustration
A, knowing that he is likely to cause the death of a pregnant woman, does an act which, if it caused the death of the woman, would amount to culpable homicide. The woman is injured but does not die; but the death of an unborn quick child with which she is pregnant thereby caused. A is guilty of the offence defined in this section.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.317.title: Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years by parent or person having care of it

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years by parent or person having care of it: 317.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years by parent or person having care of it.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.317.full_text:
317. Whoever being the father or mother of a child under the age of twelve years, or having the care of such child, shall expose or leave such child in any place with the intention of wholly abandoning such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
Explanation.This section is not intended to prevent the trial of the offender for murder or culpable homicide, as the case may be, if the child die in consequence of the exposure.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.318.title: Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body: 318.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.318.full_text: 318. Whoever, by secretly burying or otherwise disposing of the dead body of a child whether such child die before or after or during its birth, intentionally conceals or endeavours to conceal the birth of such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.319.title: Hurt

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Hurt: 319.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding hurt.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.319.full_text: 319. Whoever causes bodily pain, disease or infirmity to any person is said to cause hurt.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.320.title: Grievous hurt

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Grievous hurt: 320.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding grievous hurt.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.320.full_text:
320. The following kinds of hurt only are designated as "grievous":-
Firstly.-Emasculation.
Secondly.-Permanent privation of the sight of either eye.
Thirdly.-Permanent privation of the hearing of either ear.
Fourthly.-Privation of any member or joint.
 
 
Fifthly.-Destruction or permanent impairing of the powers of any member or joint.
 
 
Sixthly.-Permanent disfiguration of the head or face.
Seventhly.-Fracture or dislocation of a bone or tooth.
Eighthly.-Any hurt which endangers life or which causes the sufferer to be during the space of twenty days in severe bodily pain, or unable to follow his ordinary pursuits.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.321.title: Voluntarily causing hurt

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Voluntarily causing hurt: 321.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding voluntarily causing hurt.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.321.full_text: 321. Whoever does any act with the intention of thereby causing hurt to any person, or with the knowledge that he is likely thereby to cause hurt to any person, and does thereby cause hurt to any person, is said "voluntarily to cause hurt".

BD-PENAL-1860:s.322.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt

summary.one_week_summary: Penal Code 1860 - Voluntarily causing grievous hurt: 322.
summary.operative_rule: Mandates operative compliance under Penal Code 1860 regarding voluntarily causing grievous hurt.
exceptions: Statutory exceptions apply as specified in the enactment.

BD-PENAL-1860:s.322.full_text:
